You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

terial uncured breach exceeding 60 days, and cessation of product support; and

of the licensed adapter weights post-termination.

k while preserving TechNova's ownership position in brackets as an alternativ=
e.

Understood that Meridian needs time for internal review with product, enginee=
ring, and insurance. However, I want to flag that this is a critical provisio=
n for TechNova. We are integrating MeridianIQ outputs directly into a consume=
r-facing lending platform, and the risk allocation on downstream third-party =
claims needs to be addressed squarely in the agreement.

culation on May 16. I want to be transparent: without adequate AI-output inde=
mnity coverage, TechNova would need to revisit the overall risk allocation fr=
amework, including the liability cap and super-cap structure we've been discu=
ssing. These provisions do not exist in isolation.

om for compromise, but I'm not in a position to float a specific number until=

pril 21, 2025) as the base document, with Draft 2 tracked changes accepted to=
produce a clean base, and will show K&Y's new tracked changes against that c=
lean version. The markup will incorporate agreed positions, propose compromis=
e language on partially resolved items, and flag remaining open issues with a=
nnotations. We would ask that Meridian and Capstone Bridger turn comments pro=
mptly upon receipt to maintain the June 15 execution target.

1. AI-output indemnity
2. Governing law / dispute resolution
3. Liability cap / super-cap
4. De-identified data certification requirement
5. Tech E&O insurance limits
6. Latency and accuracy SLA targets
7. SLA credit cap
8. Escrow agent selection and scope

g poll early next week.
We've made good progress this week, Simone, and I appreciate the substantive =
engagement from your side. It's important that we maintain this momentum =E2=
=80=94 the initial term commencement on July 1, 2025, and Go-Live on October =
1, 2025, don't leave us a lot of runway for extended back-and-forth on the re=
maining open items. Let's aim to close as much as we can in the next two week=
s.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Definition of Confidential Information**

\"**Confidential Information**\" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the \"**Disclosing Party**\") to the other Party (the \"**Receiving Party**\") in connection with this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, and whether or not marked or designated as \"confidential,\" \"proprietary,\" or with any similar legend, that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Confidential Information includes: (a) business plans, strategies, forecasts, and financial information; (b) technical information, including source code, algorithms, model architectures, model weights, training data, APIs, and system designs; (c) trade secrets; (d) customer lists, supplier lists, and pricing information; (e) product roadmaps and development plans; and (f) the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including all pricing, fee, and commercial terms. Customer Data shall be deemed Confidential Information of Customer regardless of whether it is marked or designated as confidential.

Confidential Information shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or breach by the Receiving Party; (ii) was already known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records; (iii) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality owed to the Disclosing Party; or (iv) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records.

**Section 7.2 --- Obligations**

The Receiving Party shall: (a) hold the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) not disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted under Section 7.3; (c) use the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement; and (d) protect the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information using measures that are no less protective than those used by the Receiving Party to protect its own most sensitive confidential information, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.

The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 7 shall remain in effect during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the date of disclosure; provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.

**Section 7.3 --- Permitted Disclosures**

The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, advisors, and Affiliates who have a legitimate need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 7 (collectively, \"**Authorized Recipients**\"). The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 7 by its Authorized Recipients.

The Receiving Party may also disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal process, provided that the Receiving Party: (a) provides the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permitted) so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party\'s expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) discloses only the minimum amount of Confidential Information necessary to comply with such requirement. Any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to a legal compulsion shall retain its confidential status for all other purposes under this Agreement.

\[ADDED: \### Section 7.4 --- Injunctive Relief

Each Party acknowledges that a breach of this Article 7 may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, each Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting a bond or other security.\]

**[ARTICLE 8 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Mutual Representations and Warranties**

Each Party hereby represents and warrants to the other Party as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Effective Date that:

> \(a\) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its formation;
>
> \(b\) it has full corporate or limited liability company power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder;
>
> \(c\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or limited liability company action;
>
> \(d\) this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity; and
>
> \(e\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Party\'s organizational documents, (ii) violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Party is a party or by which it is bound.

**Section 8.2 --- Vendor Representations and Warranties**

Vendor hereby represents and warrants to Customer that:

> \(a\) the Platform, when used in accordance with the Documentation and this Agreement, will perform materially in accordance with the functional specifications set forth in the Documentation during the Term;
>
> \(b\) the Implementation Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, consistent with generally accepted industry standards for similar services, using personnel with the requisite skill, experience, and qualifications;
>
> \(c\) Vendor has all rights necessary to grant the license set forth in Section 2.1, free and clear of any liens, encumbrances, or restrictions that would materially impair Customer\'s exercise of the rights granted thereunder;
>
> \(d\) Customer\'s authorized use of the Platform as contemplated by this Agreement does not and will not infringe, misappropriate, or otherwise violate any Intellectual Property Rights of any third party;
>
> \(e\) the Platform and all services provided hereunder will comply with all applicable laws, including GLBA and CCPA/CPRA;
>
> \(f\) Vendor will maintain all insurance coverages required by Article 12 during the Term and for two (2) years thereafter; and
>
> \(g\) no open-source software included in the Platform is licensed under terms that would require Customer to disclose or distribute its proprietary software or Customer Data (e.g., no copyleft obligations that flow through to Customer\'s use).

Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any breach of the warranty set forth in Section 8.2(a) shall be for Vendor, at its option, to (i) repair or replace the non-conforming Platform functionality so that it conforms to the Documentation, or (ii) if Vendor is unable to repair or replace such functionality within a commercially reasonable period, terminate this Agreement and refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Fees attributable to the period following such termination.

**Section 8.3 --- Disclaimer**

EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 8, VENDOR MAKES NO WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE, WITH RESPECT TO THE PLATFORM, THE IMPLEMENTATION SERVICES, THE BASE MODEL, ANY DERIVATIVE MODELS, OR ANY OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, TITLE, ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS, RELIABILITY, OR QUALITY OF OUTPUTS. VENDOR DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE PLATFORM WILL BE ERROR-FREE, UNINTERRUPTED, OR FREE OF HARMFUL COMPONENTS, OR THAT THE OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM WILL BE ACCURATE, COMPLETE, OR SUITABLE FOR ANY PARTICULAR PURPOSE. CUSTOMER ACKNOWLEDGES THAT LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS ARE PROBABILISTIC IN NATURE AND THAT OUTPUTS MAY CONTAIN ERRORS, HALLUCINATIONS, OR INACCURACIES, AND CUSTOMER IS SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR EVALUATING AND VALIDATING ALL OUTPUTS FOR ITS INTENDED USE.

**[ARTICLE 9 --- SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

Vendor shall maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the \"**Uptime SLA**\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:

> **Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100**

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).

Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice to Customer\'s designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.

**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.

**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.

During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.

**Section 9.4 --- Service Credits**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"**Service Credit**\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred.

Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer\'s next invoice(s) under this Agreement . If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed thirty percent (30%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. Service Credits are not Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5.

\[ADDED: \### Section 9.5 --- Termination for Chronic SLA Failure

If Vendor fails to meet any SLA target (Uptime, Latency, or Accuracy) for three (3) or more consecutive calendar months, Customer shall have the right to terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice, without payment of any early termination fee, and Vendor shall refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Annual Platform Fees for the period following the effective date of termination.\]

**Section 9.\[DELETED: 5\] \[ADDED: 6\] --- Reporting**

**Section 2.1 --- License Grant**

Subject to and conditioned upon Customer\'s compliance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including timely payment of all Fees, Vendor hereby grants to Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable(except as permitted under Section 14.4), non-sublicensable (except to Affiliates) license during the Term to access and use the Platform solely for Customer\'s internal business operations in connection with Customer\'s lending technology product known as LendStream. The license granted hereunder includes the right to access and use the Platform through the APIs provided by Vendor, to submit Customer Data for processing through the Platform, and to receive and use the outputs generated by the Platform in connection with LendStream. In consideration of the license and access rights granted hereunder, Customer shall pay to Vendor an annual platform fee of Two Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,400,000) per Contract Year (the \"**Annual Platform Fee**\"). The Annual Platform Fee shall be invoiced by Vendor in equal monthly installments of Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$200,000) per month, with each monthly invoice due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice. **Section 4.3 --- Overage Fees**

The Annual Platform Fee includes forty million (40,000,000) API calls per Contract Year (the \"**Included API Calls**\"). API calls made by Customer in excess of the Included API Calls during any Contract Year shall be invoiced by Vendor at a rate of twelve-thousandths of a dollar (\$0.012) per API call (the \"**Overage Rate**\"). Overage Fees shall be invoiced monthly in arrears, based on Vendor\'s metering and usage data for the applicable calendar month. Each such invoice shall include a summary of API call usage for the month, including the number of API calls consumed and the number of remaining Included API Calls for the applicable Contract Year. Overage Fee invoices shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice.

All Fees set forth in this Agreement are exclusive of any and all applicable taxes, duties, levies, or similar governmental charges (collectively, \"**Taxes**\"). Customer shall be responsible for, and shall pay, all sales, use, value-added, goods and services, withholding, and similar Taxes imposed on or in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, excluding taxes based on Vendor\'s net income, capital, or franchise taxes assessed against Vendor. If Vendor is required by law to collect any Taxes from Customer, Vendor shall include such Taxes on the applicable invoice and Customer shall remit payment of such Taxes together with the applicable Fees. If Customer is required to withhold any Taxes from amounts payable to Vendor, Customer shall gross up the payment so that Vendor receives the full amount of the invoiced Fees after deduction of such withholding Taxes.

Any undisputed Fees not paid when due shall accrue interest at the lesser of (a) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (18% per annum) or (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the date such payment was due until the date such payment is received in full by Vendor. In addition, Vendor may, upon at least fifteen (15) days\' prior written notice to Customer, suspend Customer\'s access to the Platform if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid for more than forty-five (45) days past its due date, and such suspension shall continue until all outstanding amounts, including accrued interest, have been paid in full. The foregoing remedies are in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other remedies available to Vendor under this Agreement or applicable law.

**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

Vendor shall maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the \"**Uptime SLA**\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).

Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice to Customer\'s designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.
**Section 9.4 --- Service Credits**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"**Service Credit**\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred.

Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer\'s next invoice(s) under this Agreement . If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed thirty percent (30%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. Service Credits are not Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5.

**2.1 --- Classification Framework**

**Green (Preferred Position).** The Green tier represents TechNova\'s standard opening position on each negotiation term. This is the position that should be proposed in every initial draft of a vendor agreement. Acceptance of a Green-tier position by the vendor requires no escalation and no additional approval beyond the negotiating attorney\'s standard authority. The Green position represents TechNova\'s optimal outcome and should be pursued vigorously before any fallback is offered.

**Yellow (Acceptable Fallback).** The Yellow tier represents a concession that falls within an acceptable range below TechNova\'s preferred position. A Yellow-tier concession is one that in-house counsel at the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions level may approve without further escalation. The Yellow tier defines the outer boundary of what TechNova considers a commercially reasonable compromise on a given term. Negotiating attorneys should document the business rationale for accepting a Yellow-tier position in the negotiation file but are not required to seek approval from the VP Legal or General Counsel.

**Red (Walk-Away / Escalation Required).** The Red tier represents a concession that approaches or breaches TechNova\'s minimum acceptable threshold on a given term. A Red-tier position is one that the Company should ordinarily decline. If a negotiating attorney determines that acceptance of a Red-tier position may be warranted by extraordinary business circumstances, that acceptance requires written approval from the VP Legal prior to execution of the agreement. **3.1 --- Preferred Position (Green)**

**Ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations.** TechNova owns all model artifacts that are derived from or trained on TechNova\'s data, including but not limited to: fine-tuned weights, adapter layers (including LoRA and QLoRA adapters), embeddings, vector representations, and any derivative models that incorporate TechNova data in any form (collectively, \"Customer-Trained Adaptations\"). This ownership extends to all rights, title, and interest in and to the Customer-Trained Adaptations, including all intellectual property rights therein, and such ownership vests automatically upon creation without the need for any further action or assignment.

**Vendor Retention of Base Model IP.** The vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing base model (the \"Base Model\") and all platform intellectual property that existed prior to the engagement or that is developed by the vendor independently of TechNova\'s data and without use of TechNova\'s confidential information. For the avoidance of doubt, the vendor\'s retained ownership does not extend to any Customer-Trained Adaptations, regardless of whether such adaptations are implemented on or integrated with the vendor\'s Base Model.

**License to Base Model.** TechNova receives an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, fully sublicensable license to the vendor\'s Base Model solely as necessary to operate, deploy, maintain, and update the Customer-Trained Adaptations. This license survives expiration or termination of the agreement for any reason and includes the right to use the Base Model in production environments, disaster recovery environments, and development and testing environments as reasonably necessary for the operation of the Customer-Trained Adaptations.

**Portability.** The vendor must provide an API-based or otherwise automated export of all Customer-Trained Adaptations in an industry-standard format (e.g., ONNX, SafeTensors, or other format mutually agreed upon at contract execution) within thirty (30) days of the termination or expiration of the agreement. **[Section 4 --- Data Processing & Privacy]{.underline}**
**4.1 --- Regulatory Framework**

**Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (\"GLBA\").** TechNova is a financial institution within the meaning of the GLBA and its implementing regulations, including the FTC\'s Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314). Any AI/ML vendor that receives, processes, stores, or otherwise has access to NPPI in connection with the provision of services to TechNova must comply with the GLBA\'s privacy and safeguarding requirements, including the obligation to maintain an information security program that meets the standards prescribed by the Safeguards Rule.

**California Consumer Privacy Act / California Privacy Rights Act (\"CCPA/CPRA\").** TechNova processes the personal information of California residents and is subject to the CCPA, as amended by the CPRA, and the regulations promulgated thereunder by the California Privacy Protection Agency (\"CPPA\"). All AI/ML vendor agreements involving access to personal information of California residents must comply with the CCPA/CPRA\'s requirements for service-provider relationships, including the contractual certifications and restrictions described in Section 4.2 below.
**4.2 --- Mandatory Requirements (All Zones --- Non-Negotiable)**

**Service-Provider / Processor Designation.** The vendor must contractually agree to act as a \"service provider\" as defined in California Civil Code Section 1798.140(ag) with respect to all personal information of California residents that the vendor receives, processes, or accesses in connection with the agreement. Where applicable, the vendor must also agree to act as a \"processor\" under the GLBA and its implementing regulations, and to comply with all obligations imposed on processors under those regulations. This designation is mandatory and non-negotiable. A vendor that refuses to accept a service-provider designation, or that insists on being treated as an independent \"business\" or \"controller\" with respect to TechNova customer data, presents a fundamental compliance risk that cannot be mitigated through other contractual mechanisms.

**Data Processing Agreement (DPA).** Every AI/ML vendor agreement must include a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) as an exhibit, schedule, or appendix to the agreement, or as a standalone agreement executed concurrently with the vendor agreement. The DPA must contain, at minimum, the following provisions:

**Prohibition on Third-Party Model Training.** The vendor must be contractually prohibited from using TechNova customer data --- including any derivatives, transformations, embeddings, or representations thereof --- for training, improving, fine-tuning, or otherwise enhancing any models or algorithms for the benefit of third parties or for the benefit of the vendor\'s general-purpose product offerings. This prohibition must extend to all forms of the data, including de-identified or aggregated forms, unless a specific de-identification right has been negotiated in accordance with Section 4.3 below. This prohibition is absolute and non-negotiable.
**4.3 --- De-Identification Standards**

**Statutory Standard.** The de-identification must meet the statutory standard set forth in the CCPA at California Civil Code Section 1798.140(m). Specifically, the information must be information that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, a particular consumer or household, provided that the vendor (a) has implemented technical safeguards and business processes that prohibit re-identification of the consumer to whom the information may pertain; (b) has implemented business processes to prevent inadvertent release of de-identified information; and (c) makes no attempt to re-identify the information.

**Independent Third-Party Verification.** The de-identification process and its compliance with the statutory standard must be verified by an independent third-party auditor. The auditor must be approved by TechNova in writing prior to the commencement of any audit. The auditor must provide a written certification that the de-identification meets the statutory standard, and this certification must be provided to TechNova before the vendor may make any use of the de-identified data.

**Classification.** Any de-identification right is within the Yellow zone only if both conditions above (statutory standard compliance and independent verification) are satisfied in full. If the vendor proposes a de-identification right without independent third-party verification, or if the proposed de-identification standard does not meet the CCPA statutory standard, the concession falls within the Red zone and requires VP Legal approval before acceptance.

**Minimum (Non-Negotiable).** The vendor must commit to a monthly uptime percentage of at least 99.95%, measured across all production endpoints made available to TechNova under the agreement. **6.2 --- Latency**

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred latency commitment is a p95 response latency of no more than four hundred milliseconds (≤ 400 ms), measured at the vendor\'s API gateway for production inference requests. **Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred model accuracy commitment is an F1 score of at least 0.95 on agreed benchmark datasets. **Red (Walk-Away).** Any accuracy commitment below an F1 score of 0.92 is a walk-away. A vendor that cannot commit to at least F1 ≥ 0.92 on agreed benchmark datasets is not able to meet TechNova\'s minimum performance requirements.

Every AI/ML vendor agreement entered into by TechNova must be negotiated consistent with the positions, fallbacks, and walk-away thresholds set forth herein. Specifically, the information must be information that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, a particular consumer or household, provided that the vendor (a) has implemented technical safeguards and business processes that prohibit re-identification of the consumer to whom the information may pertain; (b) has implemented business processes to prevent inadvertent release of de-identified information; and (c) makes no attempt to re-identify the information.

**Classification.** Any de-identification right is within the Yellow zone only if both conditions above (statutory standard compliance and independent verification) are satisfied in full. If the vendor proposes a de-identification right without independent third-party verification, or if the proposed de-identification standard does not meet the CCPA statutory standard, the concession falls within the Red zone and requires VP Legal approval before acceptance.

The service-provider designation and the DPA with CCPA certification are foundational compliance requirements. These terms must appear in every AI/ML vendor agreement and must not be traded for concessions in other areas of the negotiation --- not for more favorable pricing, not for enhanced SLAs, and not for any other commercial benefit.

If a vendor proposes a \"controller-to-controller\" or \"independent contractor\" data relationship --- in which the vendor would process TechNova customer data as an independent business or controller with its own rights to use the data --- this is a walk-away absent extraordinary circumstances approved by the General Counsel. A controller-to-controller relationship would expose TechNova to significant regulatory risk under both the GLBA and the CCPA/CPRA, including potential liability for the vendor\'s independent use of customer data, and would undermine TechNova\'s ability to comply with its own privacy obligations to its customers.
**[Section 5 --- Liability Framework]{.underline}**
**5.1 --- General Liability Cap**

The general limitation of liability in any AI/ML vendor agreement sets the maximum aggregate amount that the vendor may be required to pay to TechNova (and vice versa) for all claims arising under the agreement, subject to the carve-outs described in Section 5.2. The following thresholds apply:

Be alert to vendor proposals that use trailing-fee-based caps rather than annual-fee-based caps. Some vendors will propose caps based on the fees paid or payable during the preceding six-month or twelve-month period (e.g., \"not to exceed the fees paid by Customer in the six months preceding the claim\"). If the vendor proposes a trailing-fee-based cap, convert the proposed cap to its annual-fee equivalent and evaluate it against the thresholds set forth above. A cap based on six months of trailing fees, for example, is equivalent to approximately 0.5× annual fees and would fall below the Red-zone floor.
**[Section 6 --- Service Level Agreements (SLAs)]{.underline}**

**Minimum (Non-Negotiable).** The vendor must commit to a monthly uptime percentage of at least 99.95%, measured across all production endpoints made available to TechNova under the agreement. This equates to a maximum permissible downtime of approximately 21 minutes and 54 seconds per month. This threshold is non-negotiable and applies to all AI/ML vendor engagements regardless of the business unit, use case, or TCV.

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred latency commitment is a p95 response latency of no more than four hundred milliseconds (≤ 400 ms), measured at the vendor\'s API gateway for production inference requests. This threshold is required for real-time, customer-facing applications, including the LendStream product line and any other deployment that involves real-time decisioning, scoring, or response generation in interaction with end users.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** If the vendor cannot commit to ≤ 400 ms p95 latency, TechNova will accept a p95 response latency of no more than five hundred milliseconds (≤ 500 ms). A vendor offer in the range of 401--500 ms falls within the acceptable zone but below the preferred threshold. Negotiating attorneys should make a good-faith effort to secure a commitment at or below 400 ms before accepting a latency commitment in the 401--500 ms range.

If the vendor\'s best offer falls within the 401--500 ms range (e.g., 450 ms p95), the negotiating attorney should flag the offer to Product Engineering for confirmation that the specific use case can tolerate the additional latency. For example, a 450 ms commitment may be acceptable for batch processing or non-time-critical analytics, but may not be acceptable for LendStream real-time decisioning, where even 50 ms of additional latency can materially affect conversion rates and customer experience. Product Engineering confirmation should be documented in the negotiation file before the concession is accepted.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any latency commitment above 500 ms p95 is a walk-away for customer-facing AI deployments. This threshold applies to any deployment that directly serves or interacts with TechNova\'s customers in real time. For internal-only, non-customer-facing deployments (e.g., internal analytics, back-office model inference), the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions may approve a latency commitment above 500 ms on a case-by-case basis, subject to Product Engineering\'s written confirmation that the higher latency does not impact customer experience.

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred model accuracy commitment is an F1 score of at least 0.95 on agreed benchmark datasets. The benchmark datasets must be mutually agreed upon at the time of contract execution and must be representative of TechNova\'s production data distribution. The F1 score should be calculated on the basis of the agreed evaluation methodology, including the specific precision and recall definitions applicable to TechNova\'s use case.

**Yellow (Acceptable).** TechNova will accept a model accuracy commitment with an F1 score of at least 0.92 on agreed benchmark datasets. An F1 score of 0.92 is the Playbook minimum; no accuracy commitment below this threshold is acceptable without escalation.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any accuracy commitment below an F1 score of 0.92 is a walk-away. A vendor that cannot commit to at least F1 ≥ 0.92 on agreed benchmark datasets is not able to meet TechNova\'s minimum performance requirements.

Where a vendor proposes a post-deployment ramp period (e.g., a 90-day stabilization period during which the model is tuned to TechNova\'s production data), the following approach is acceptable: the ramp target may begin at the Yellow floor (F1 ≥ 0.92) at the commencement of the stabilization period, provided that the agreement requires the vendor to achieve the preferred threshold (F1 ≥ 0.95, or such other post-stabilization target as may be negotiated) by the end of the stabilization period. If the vendor fails to achieve the post-stabilization target by the end of the ramp period, TechNova must have the right to terminate the agreement without penalty.

**Green (Preferred).** TechNova\'s preferred position on service credits is that credits should be calculated as a meaningful percentage of the monthly fees payable under the agreement, with a credit cap of at least thirty percent (30%) of monthly fees per month. The credit schedule should provide graduated credits tied to the severity of the SLA breach (e.g., 10% credit for uptime between 99.90% and 99.95%; 20% credit for uptime between 99.50% and 99.89%; 30% credit for uptime below 99.50%).

Every AI/ML vendor agreement must include a termination right that may be exercised by TechNova in the event of chronic SLA underperformance. Chronic underperformance is defined as a material SLA miss --- including uptime, latency, or accuracy failures --- in three (3) or more consecutive calendar months.

For latency, the negotiating attorney should push firmly for a commitment at or below 400 ms p95, especially for any deployment supporting the LendStream platform or other real-time consumer-facing products. If the vendor counters with a latency commitment between 400 ms and 500 ms, the negotiating attorney should coordinate with the VP of Product Engineering (currently Priya Anand) before accepting. Product Engineering\'s assessment of whether the specific use case can tolerate the proposed latency should be documented in the negotiation file.

For accuracy, an F1 score of 0.92 is the absolute minimum; the preferred threshold is 0.95. A stabilization ramp period is acceptable only if the post-stabilization target meets or exceeds the preferred threshold, and only if the agreement provides TechNova with a termination right if the target is not achieved by the end of the ramp period.
**[Section 7 --- Source Code / Model Escrow]{.underline}**
**7.1 --- Escrow Threshold**

Escrow is mandatory for any AI/ML vendor engagement with a total contract value (\"TCV\") exceeding one million dollars (\$1,000,000). The TCV calculation includes all fees payable under the agreement over the initial term, including platform fees, implementation fees, usage-based fees (estimated at projected usage), and any other fees or charges payable to the vendor.
**7.3 --- Preferred Escrow Agent**

A complete list of approved and acceptable escrow agents is maintained in Appendix B. Escrow agent selection should be proposed by TechNova in the initial draft of the agreement. If the vendor proposes an alternative agent, the negotiating attorney should evaluate the proposed agent against the selection criteria set forth in Appendix B and consult with the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions if the proposed agent is not already on the approved list.
**8.1 --- Commercial General Liability (CGL)**
**8.2 --- Technology Errors & Omissions (Tech E&O)**

**Yellow (Acceptable / Minimum).** For all AI/ML vendor engagements (regardless of TCV), the minimum acceptable Tech E&O coverage is five million dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence. This is the absolute floor for Tech E&O coverage.

**Red (Walk-Away).** Any Tech E&O coverage below \$5,000,000 per occurrence is a walk-away. Acceptance of a Tech E&O limit below \$5,000,000 requires VP Legal approval with a documented risk assessment.

For engagements with a TCV exceeding \$5,000,000, negotiating attorneys should push firmly for the \$10,000,000 preferred limit. If the vendor\'s current policy limit is \$5,000,000, explore whether the vendor is willing to obtain an endorsement, policy amendment, or increased limits as a condition of the agreement. The cost of increased coverage should be borne by the vendor and should not be passed through to TechNova. If the vendor demonstrates that \$10,000,000 in Tech E&O coverage is not commercially available or is prohibitively expensive, the negotiating attorney should escalate to the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions with a written risk assessment before accepting the \$5,000,000 minimum.
**8.3 --- Umbrella / Excess Liability**

Every AI/ML vendor must maintain umbrella or excess liability insurance with a minimum limit of ten million dollars (\$10,000,000). This coverage must sit excess of the vendor\'s CGL and Tech E&O policies and must provide coverage for claims that exceed the underlying policy limits.

If a vendor resists the \$10,000,000 Tech E&O requirement for a high-TCV deal, the negotiating attorney should escalate to the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions with a risk assessment that considers: (a) the TCV and duration of the engagement; (b) the nature of the vendor\'s services and the potential magnitude of technology-related claims; (c) the vendor\'s financial condition and balance sheet strength; and (d) the availability of other contractual protections (e.g., liability caps, indemnification, escrow) that may partially mitigate the risk. Only after this assessment should a decision be made to accept the \$5,000,000 minimum.

No other carve-outs to the vendor\'s AI-output indemnity obligation are acceptable without the express approval of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions. In particular, negotiating attorneys should be alert to vendor proposals that attempt to carve out liability for \"model hallucinations,\" \"accuracy limitations,\" or \"inherent limitations of AI technology.\" Such carve-outs are overbroad and would effectively eliminate the vendor\'s indemnity obligation for the most common categories of AI-output claims.

> \(a\) **Litigation Carve-Out.** Negotiate a carve-out providing that disputes with an amount in controversy exceeding \$1,000,000 shall be resolved by litigation in the agreed forum (Delaware, New York, or Texas courts), with arbitration applicable only to disputes below the \$1,000,000 threshold.
**[Section 11 --- Indemnification]{.underline}**
**11.1 --- Scope of IP Indemnity**
**11.2 --- Standard Indemnity Obligations**

**Vendor\'s Indemnification of TechNova.** The vendor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless TechNova and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all third-party claims, losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from or relating to:

**TechNova\'s Indemnification of Vendor.** TechNova will indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the vendor and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all third-party claims, losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from or relating to:
**11.3 --- Indemnity Procedures**

> • **Version 3.2 --- March 2025.** Current version. Updates include: (a) revisions to the AI-Output Risk Allocation section (Section 9) to address emerging vendor indemnity requirements and market developments related to generative AI outputs, including the addition of the shared-risk framework as an acceptable fallback position; (b) updates to the Data Processing & Privacy section (Section 4) to reflect regulatory developments under the CPRA and the California Privacy Protection Agency\'s rulemaking activities, including enhanced de-identification standards; and (c) updates to the Liability Framework (Section 5) to clarify the mechanics of the super-cap for IP indemnity and data breach carve-outs, including illustrative dollar-amount examples.

> • **Version 3.1 --- September 2024.** Added escrow requirements for AI/ML model artifacts (Section 7); updated insurance requirements for Tech E&O coverage (Section 8); added Appendix B (Approved Escrow Agents).
> • **Version 2.0 --- September 2023.** Added Data Processing & Privacy section (Section 4) to address CCPA/CPRA compliance; updated SLA provisions (Section 6).

**WHEREAS,** the Parties have entered into the Agreement referenced above, pursuant to which Vendor provides certain services to Company (also referred to herein as \"TechNova\") or its affiliates, as more fully described in the Agreement;

**[Article 1 --- Definitions]{.underline}**

Civ. Code § 1798.100 *et seq.*), as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020 (\"CPRA\"); (b) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (15 U.S.C. § 6801 *et seq.*) and its implementing regulations, including the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314); (c) the California Financial Information Privacy Act (Cal. Fin. Code § 4050 *et seq.*); (d) any other applicable state consumer privacy statutes; and (e) all regulations, guidance, and opinions issued by competent regulatory authorities interpreting any of the foregoing, in each case as amended, superseded, or replaced from time to time.
**1.2 \"Business\"** has the meaning ascribed to such term under CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(d), and as used in this DPA refers to Company.

**1.3 \"Business Purpose\"** has the meaning ascribed to such term under CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(e), and refers to the specific purposes for which Personal Information is disclosed by Company to Vendor, as described in Exhibit C attached hereto. For the avoidance of doubt, \"Business Purpose\" includes any use of Personal Information that is necessary to perform the services set forth in the Agreement, including auditing, detecting security incidents, debugging, short-term transient use, performing services on behalf of Company, internal research for technological development, and activities to verify or maintain the quality or safety of a service, all as further described in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(e).

The term \"Consumer\" includes \"Data Subject\" where applicable under Applicable Data Protection Laws, and shall be construed broadly to encompass any individual afforded rights with respect to their Personal Information under any Applicable Data Protection Law.

**1.5 \"Controller\"** means the entity that, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of Processing Personal Information. As used in this DPA, \"Controller\" refers to Company.

**1.6 \"Data Breach\"** means any unauthorized access to, or unauthorized acquisition, disclosure, use, destruction, alteration, or loss of, Personal Information, whether in electronic or physical form, including any \"breach of the security of the system\" as defined under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.29 and Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.82, and any event that triggers notification obligations under any Applicable Data Protection Law. The term \"Data Breach\" encompasses both confirmed breaches and reasonably suspected breaches.

**1.7 \"De-Identified Data\"** means information that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, a particular Consumer or household, provided that a business that uses De-Identified Data: (a) has implemented technical safeguards that prohibit re-identification of the Consumer to whom the information may pertain; (b) has implemented business processes that specifically prohibit re-identification of the information; (c) has implemented business processes to prevent inadvertent release of De-Identified Data; and (d) makes no attempt to re-identify the information, all in accordance with the requirements of Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and as further described in Article 10 of this DPA.
