Part 314), the Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards, and any successor regulations or amendments thereto.

**1.9 \"Personal Information\"** means information that identifies, relates to, describes, is reasonably capable of being associated with, or could reasonably be linked, directly or indirectly, with a particular Consumer or household, as defined under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(v). The term \"Personal Information\" also includes \"Nonpublic Personal Information\" as defined under GLBA (15 U.S.C. § 6809(4)) and its implementing regulations, where such information is Processed in connection with the services provided under the Agreement. Personal Information does not include publicly available information, De-Identified Data, or aggregate consumer information, to the extent such exclusions are recognized under Applicable Data Protection Laws.

**1.10 \"Processing\"** (and \"Process,\" \"Processed\") means any operation or set of operations that is performed on Personal Information or on sets of Personal Information, whether or not by automated means, including but not limited to collection, recording, organization, structuring, storage, adaptation, alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination, or otherwise making available, alignment, combination, restriction, erasure, or destruction, as referenced in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(y).

**1.11 \"Processor\"** means an entity that Processes Personal Information on behalf of the Controller. As used in this DPA, \"Processor\" refers to Vendor in its capacity as a service provider under the Agreement.

**1.12 \"Service Provider\"** has the meaning ascribed to such term under CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), and refers to Vendor in its capacity under the Agreement. For purposes of this DPA, Vendor is a Service Provider that receives Personal Information from Company for a Business Purpose pursuant to a written contract that satisfies the requirements of the CCPA and CPRA.

**1.13 \"Sub-Processor\"** means any third party (other than Vendor\'s employees) engaged by Vendor to Process Personal Information on behalf of Company in connection with the services provided under the Agreement. A Sub-Processor includes any subcontractor, agent, or other downstream service provider to which Vendor delegates any portion of the Processing activities contemplated under this DPA.

**1.14 \"Technical and Organizational Measures\"** or **\"TOMs\"** means the administrative, technical, and physical security measures implemented by Vendor to protect Personal Information against unauthorized or unlawful Processing and against accidental loss, destruction, damage, alteration, or disclosure, as more fully described in Exhibit A to this DPA.

**1.15 Incorporation of Agreement Definitions.** All terms defined in the Agreement that are used but not separately defined in this DPA shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement. In the event of any conflict between the definitions set forth in this DPA and the definitions set forth in the Agreement, the definitions in this DPA shall control with respect to matters relating to the Processing of Personal Information.
**[Article 2 --- Roles and Scope of Processing]{.underline}**

**2.1 Designation of Roles.** With respect to Personal Information Processed under the Agreement, Company shall act as the Business and Controller, and Vendor shall act as the Service Provider and Processor. Each Party shall comply with the obligations applicable to it in its respective role under Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor acknowledges and agrees that it is a \"service provider\" as defined under the CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), and shall act in accordance with the duties and restrictions applicable to service providers under the CCPA and CPRA.

**2.2 Purpose Limitation.** Vendor shall Process Personal Information solely on behalf of Company and only for the specific Business Purposes identified in Exhibit C to this DPA. Vendor shall not Process Personal Information for any purpose that is incompatible with the Business Purposes specified herein without the prior written consent of Company. Any additional Processing activities beyond those described in Exhibit C shall require a written amendment to this DPA executed by both Parties in accordance with Section 14.3.

**2.3 Processing Description.** The subject matter, duration, nature, and purpose of Processing, the categories of Personal Information Processed, and the categories of Consumers whose Personal Information is Processed are described in Exhibit C (Processing Description) attached to this DPA. Exhibit C is incorporated herein by reference and forms an integral part of this DPA. Company may update Exhibit C from time to time in writing to reflect changes in the scope of services under the Agreement, and Vendor shall comply with any such updates promptly upon receipt.

**2.4 No Consideration for Personal Information.** Vendor acknowledges and agrees that it does not receive Personal Information as consideration for the services provided under the Agreement. Personal Information is disclosed by Company to Vendor solely for the Business Purposes described in this DPA and Exhibit C. The exchange of Personal Information does not constitute a \"sale\" or \"sharing\" of Personal Information within the meaning of the CCPA or CPRA.

**2.5 No Ownership Interest.** Nothing in this DPA or the Agreement confers upon Vendor any ownership interest, license, or other proprietary right in or to the Personal Information. Vendor acknowledges that Company retains all rights, title, and interest in and to the Personal Information at all times. Vendor\'s right to Process Personal Information is limited solely to the rights expressly granted under this DPA and the Agreement, and such right shall terminate upon the expiration or termination of the Agreement, subject to the data return and deletion obligations set forth in Article 11.
**[Article 3 --- Processing Instructions and Restrictions]{.underline}**

**3.1 Documented Instructions.** Vendor shall Process Personal Information only in accordance with Company\'s documented instructions as set forth in this DPA, Exhibit C, and any subsequent written instructions provided by Company from time to time. Company\'s initial instructions are set forth in Exhibit C and are deemed effective as of the effective date of this DPA. Vendor shall not deviate from Company\'s documented instructions without prior written authorization from Company. If Vendor believes that additional Processing is necessary for reasons other than those instructed by Company, Vendor shall promptly inform Company of such necessity before commencing such Processing, unless prohibited from doing so by Applicable Data Protection Laws, in which case Vendor shall notify Company of the relevant legal requirement to the extent permitted by law.

**3.2 Prohibition on Sale, Sharing, and Unauthorized Disclosure.** Vendor shall not sell, share, rent, release, disclose, disseminate, make available, transfer, or otherwise communicate orally, in writing, or by electronic or other means, Personal Information to any third party for any purpose other than the specific Business Purposes set forth in this DPA and the Agreement. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor shall not \"sell\" or \"share\" Personal Information, as those terms are defined in the CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.140(ad) and 1798.140(ah), respectively.

**3.3 No Unauthorized Retention, Use, or Disclosure.** Vendor shall not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information for any commercial purpose other than providing the services specified in the Agreement and for the Business Purposes identified in Exhibit C. Vendor shall not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information outside of the direct business relationship between Vendor and Company. For the avoidance of doubt, Vendor shall not use Personal Information received from Company to build or enhance profiles concerning Consumers, to advertise or market products or services to Consumers, or for any purpose unrelated to the provision of the services under the Agreement.

**3.4 Prohibition on Combining Personal Information.** Vendor shall not combine Personal Information received from, or on behalf of, Company with Personal Information that Vendor: (a) receives from, or on behalf of, another person or persons; or (b) collects from its own interaction with Consumers, except as expressly permitted under CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(e)(6), which permits combining Personal Information to the extent necessary to detect data security incidents or to protect against fraudulent or illegal activity, provided that such combining is performed solely to the extent reasonably necessary and proportionate to achieving such purposes.

**3.5 Notification of Unlawful Instructions.** Vendor shall promptly inform Company in writing if, in Vendor\'s reasonable opinion, an instruction from Company infringes Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall not be required to comply with any instruction that it reasonably believes to be unlawful, and shall await further written instructions from Company before proceeding. In the event of a disagreement between the Parties regarding the lawfulness of an instruction, the Parties shall consult in good faith to resolve the matter. Vendor shall document any notification provided under this Section and retain such documentation for the term of this DPA.

**3.6 Confidentiality of Personnel.** Vendor shall ensure that all persons authorized to Process Personal Information on Vendor\'s behalf, including employees, contractors, agents, and other personnel, have committed themselves to binding obligations of confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality. Vendor shall ensure that such personnel Process Personal Information only in accordance with Vendor\'s instructions, which shall be consistent with Company\'s instructions as set forth in this DPA. Vendor shall provide regular training to its personnel regarding the obligations imposed by this DPA and Applicable Data Protection Laws, and shall maintain records of such training.
**[Article 4 --- Sub-Processor Management]{.underline}**

**4.1 Prior Written Consent Required.** Vendor shall not engage any Sub-Processor to Process Personal Information on behalf of Company without obtaining Company\'s prior written consent. Such consent may be granted on a specific or general basis. If Company provides general authorization, Vendor shall comply with the notification and objection procedures set forth in Sections 4.3 and 4.4 below before engaging any new Sub-Processor or replacing an existing Sub-Processor.

**4.2 Approved Sub-Processors.** A list of Sub-Processors approved by Company as of the effective date of this DPA is set forth in Exhibit B. Company hereby grants specific written consent for each Sub-Processor identified in Exhibit B as of the effective date of this DPA. Vendor represents and warrants that, as of the effective date, the Sub-Processors listed in Exhibit B are the only Sub-Processors engaged by Vendor to Process Personal Information on behalf of Company.

**4.3 New Sub-Processor Notification.** Prior to engaging any new Sub-Processor or replacing an existing Sub-Processor, Vendor shall provide Company with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice. Such notice shall include: (a) the identity of the proposed Sub-Processor, including its legal name and principal place of business; (b) a description of the nature and scope of the Processing activities to be performed by the proposed Sub-Processor; (c) the location(s) where Processing will occur; and (d) an explanation of how the proposed Sub-Processor will comply with the obligations set forth in this DPA. Vendor shall update Exhibit B promptly upon the engagement of any new Sub-Processor approved by Company.

**4.4 Company Objection Rights.** Company shall have the right to object to the engagement of a proposed Sub-Processor by providing written notice of its objection to Vendor within fifteen (15) days of receiving Vendor\'s notification under Section 4.3. Company\'s objection notice shall set forth the reasonable grounds for objection. Upon receipt of an objection, the Parties shall engage in good-faith discussions to resolve the matter, which may include Vendor proposing an alternative Sub-Processor or implementing additional safeguards. If the Parties are unable to resolve the objection within thirty (30) days of Company\'s objection notice, Company shall have the right to terminate the affected services under the Agreement without penalty, liability, or early-termination fee, by providing written notice to Vendor. Such termination shall be effective upon the date specified in Company\'s termination notice, which shall be no less than thirty (30) days from the date of such notice, and Vendor shall comply with the data return and deletion obligations set forth in Article 11 with respect to the terminated services.

**4.5 Flow-Down Obligations.** Vendor shall impose on each Sub-Processor, by way of a written agreement, data protection obligations that are no less protective of Personal Information than those set forth in this DPA. Such written agreement shall include, at a minimum: (a) the obligation to Process Personal Information only in accordance with Company\'s documented instructions; (b) the obligation to implement appropriate Technical and Organizational Measures; (c) the obligation to cooperate with audits and inspections; (d) the obligation to assist in responding to Consumer rights requests; (e) Data Breach notification obligations; and (f) data return and deletion obligations upon termination. Vendor shall provide Company with copies of its Sub-Processor agreements, or relevant excerpts thereof (which may be redacted to remove commercially sensitive information not related to data protection), upon Company\'s reasonable request.

**4.6 Vendor Liability for Sub-Processors.** Vendor shall remain fully liable to Company for the acts and omissions of its Sub-Processors with respect to the Processing of Personal Information as if such acts and omissions were Vendor\'s own. Vendor\'s engagement of a Sub-Processor shall not relieve Vendor of any of its obligations under this DPA or the Agreement. If a Sub-Processor fails to fulfill its data protection obligations, Vendor shall be directly and primarily liable to Company for the performance of the Sub-Processor\'s obligations.

**4.7 Company Audit Rights over Sub-Processors.** Company\'s right to audit Sub-Processors shall be exercised in accordance with Article 12. Company may audit Sub-Processors directly or may direct Vendor to conduct such audits on Company\'s behalf and provide the results to Company. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to include in its Sub-Processor agreements provisions allowing Company or its designee to exercise audit rights over the Sub-Processor\'s Processing activities related to Company\'s Personal Information.

**5.1 General Security Obligation.** Vendor shall implement and maintain appropriate Technical and Organizational Measures to protect Personal Information against unauthorized or unlawful Processing and against accidental loss, destruction, damage, alteration, or disclosure. The TOMs shall be appropriate to the risk, taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation, and the nature, scope, context, and purposes of Processing, as well as the likelihood and severity of harm to Consumers. The specific TOMs in effect as of the effective date of this DPA are described in Exhibit A. Vendor shall ensure that such measures provide a level of security appropriate to the sensitivity of the Personal Information being Processed.
**5.2 Specific Security Requirements.** Without limiting the generality of Section 5.1, Vendor shall implement and maintain the following security measures at a minimum:

**5.3 SOC 2 Type II Certification.** Vendor shall obtain and maintain a current Service Organization Control (SOC) 2 Type II report, prepared by an independent certified public accounting firm in accordance with the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) Trust Services Criteria, covering at a minimum the Security, Availability, and Confidentiality trust services criteria. Vendor shall provide a copy of the most recent SOC 2 Type II report to Company upon execution of this DPA, and thereafter on an annual basis within thirty (30) days of Vendor\'s receipt of each updated report. Vendor shall promptly notify Company of any material exceptions, qualifications, or findings of non-compliance identified in any SOC 2 Type II report, along with Vendor\'s plans and timelines for remediation.

**5.4 Notification of Material Security Changes.** Vendor shall promptly notify Company in writing of any material changes to its Technical and Organizational Measures that may adversely affect the security, confidentiality, integrity, or availability of Personal Information. Company reserves the right to review and approve or reject any such changes, and Vendor shall not implement any material adverse change without Company\'s prior written consent.

Vendor acknowledges that compliance with the CCPA is an essential component of its obligations under this DPA and the Agreement.

**6.2 Statutory Service Provider Certification.** In accordance with the requirements of Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and the regulations promulgated thereunder, Vendor hereby certifies each of the following:

**6.3 Company\'s Right to Ensure Compliance.** Vendor grants Company the right, upon reasonable notice, to take reasonable and appropriate steps to help ensure that Vendor uses Personal Information received from Company in a manner consistent with Company\'s obligations under the CCPA and CPRA. Such steps may include, without limitation, requesting information about Vendor\'s Processing activities, conducting audits or assessments in accordance with Article 12, and requiring Vendor to implement additional safeguards or remedial measures. Vendor shall cooperate fully with Company in connection with any such steps.

**6.4 Notification of Inability to Comply.** Vendor shall promptly notify Company if Vendor determines that it can no longer meet its obligations under the CCPA or CPRA, or if any change in Applicable Data Protection Laws materially affects Vendor\'s ability to comply with its obligations under this Article. Upon receipt of such notification, Company shall have the right to take reasonable and appropriate steps to stop and remediate any unauthorized use of Personal Information, which may include directing Vendor to cease Processing Personal Information, suspending the transfer of Personal Information to Vendor, and/or terminating the Agreement or the affected services thereunder. **[Article 7 --- GLBA Safeguards Compliance]{.underline}**

**7.1 Applicability.** To the extent that Vendor receives, maintains, or Processes Personal Information that constitutes \"customer information\" or \"Nonpublic Personal Information\" as defined under GLBA and its implementing regulations, Vendor shall comply with the safeguards requirements of the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) and any other applicable GLBA requirements. The obligations set forth in this Article 7 are in addition to, and do not limit, the security obligations set forth in Article 5.

**7.2 Comprehensive Information Security Program.** Vendor shall develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive written information security program that contains administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to: (a) ensure the security and confidentiality of Nonpublic Personal Information; (b) protect against any anticipated threats or hazards to the security or integrity of such information; and (c) protect against unauthorized access to or use of such information that could result in substantial harm or inconvenience to any Consumer. The safeguards shall be appropriate to the size and complexity of Vendor\'s operations, the nature and scope of Vendor\'s activities, and the sensitivity of the Nonpublic Personal Information at issue.

**7.3 Designated Qualified Individual.** Vendor shall designate a qualified individual responsible for overseeing, implementing, and enforcing Vendor\'s information security program. The qualified individual may be an employee, affiliate, or a third-party service provider, provided that, in the case of a third-party service provider, Vendor retains overall responsibility for oversight and direction of the information security program. Vendor shall provide Company with the name, title, and contact information of the designated qualified individual upon Company\'s request.

**7.4 Periodic Risk Assessments.** Vendor shall conduct periodic risk assessments, no less frequently than annually, that: (a) identify reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of Nonpublic Personal Information that could result in the unauthorized disclosure, misuse, alteration, destruction, or other compromise of such information; (b) assess the sufficiency of any safeguards in place to control these risks; and (c) design and implement safeguards to control the risks identified through the risk assessment. Vendor shall adjust its information security program based on the results of each risk assessment and shall maintain documentation of each risk assessment and the resulting actions taken.

**7.5 Access Restriction.** Vendor shall restrict access to Nonpublic Personal Information to those authorized personnel who have a legitimate business need for such access in connection with the services provided under the Agreement. Vendor shall implement and maintain procedures for granting, modifying, and revoking access to Nonpublic Personal Information, including prompt revocation of access upon termination of employment or engagement of any authorized personnel.

**7.6 Evidence of Compliance.** Vendor shall provide evidence of its compliance with the GLBA Safeguards requirements set forth in this Article upon Company\'s reasonable request. Such evidence may include, without limitation: (a) copies of or summaries of Vendor\'s information security program; (b) results of risk assessments (which may be provided in summary or redacted form to protect Vendor\'s confidential security information); (c) evidence of security training and awareness programs; (d) certifications or attestation letters from Vendor\'s designated qualified individual; and (e) any relevant audit reports, including SOC 2 Type II reports. Vendor shall provide such evidence within thirty (30) days of Company\'s request.
**[Article 8 --- Data Breach Notification]{.underline}**

**8.1 Notification Obligation.** Vendor shall notify Company of any confirmed or reasonably suspected Data Breach involving Personal Information Processed by Vendor or its Sub-Processors on behalf of Company without undue delay and in no event later than seventy-two (72) hours after Vendor first becomes aware of such Data Breach. Vendor shall direct its notification to Company\'s Privacy Contact identified in Section 14.8, as well as any other contacts designated by Company for Data Breach notifications. Notification shall be made by telephone and confirmed in writing via email and, if available, through any incident management portal designated by Company.
**8.2 Content of Notification.** Vendor\'s notification to Company under Section 8.1 shall include, to the extent known at the time of notification and without unreasonable delay:

**8.3 Ongoing Cooperation.** Vendor shall cooperate fully with Company in investigating, remediating, and responding to any Data Breach, including: (a) providing Company with updated information regarding the Data Breach as it becomes available; (b) assisting Company in identifying affected Consumers and the Personal Information compromised; (c) supporting Company\'s regulatory filings, Consumer notifications, and other response activities; (d) preserving and producing documents, records, and other materials relevant to the Data Breach investigation; and (e) making Vendor\'s personnel, systems, and facilities reasonably available to Company and its investigators, legal counsel, and forensic consultants.

**8.4 Containment and Remediation.** Upon becoming aware of a Data Breach, Vendor shall immediately take all reasonable and necessary steps to contain, investigate, and remediate the Data Breach, including: (a) isolating affected systems; (b) preserving forensic evidence; (c) identifying the root cause; (d) eradicating the threat; (e) restoring the integrity of affected systems and data; and (f) implementing measures to prevent recurrence. All such containment, investigation, and remediation activities shall be performed at Vendor\'s sole cost and expense.

**8.5 Notification Restrictions.** Vendor shall not notify any Consumer, regulatory authority, law enforcement agency, credit reporting agency, or any other third party of a Data Breach involving Company\'s Personal Information without Company\'s prior written consent, unless Vendor is required to make such notification under Applicable Data Protection Laws, in which case Vendor shall: (a) notify Company of such legal requirement prior to making the notification, to the extent permitted by law; (b) coordinate with Company regarding the timing, content, and method of such notification; and (c) provide Company with a copy of any notification prior to its issuance, to the extent practicable.

**8.6 Preservation of Records and Evidence.** Vendor shall preserve all records, logs, files, data, communications, and other evidence related to a Data Breach in a secure and tamper-evident manner. Vendor shall not alter, destroy, or dispose of any such evidence without Company\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall make all such records and evidence available to Company and its authorized representatives upon request, at no additional cost to Company.

**8.7 Non-Exclusivity of Notification Obligations.** Vendor\'s notification obligations under this Article 8 are in addition to, and do not replace, modify, or limit, any notification obligations that Vendor may have under Applicable Data Protection Laws, the Agreement, or any other contractual arrangement between the Parties. Vendor shall comply with all notification obligations imposed by Applicable Data Protection Laws, including any obligations to notify regulatory authorities or affected individuals within the timeframes prescribed by law.
**[Article 9 --- Data Subject / Consumer Rights Cooperation]{.underline}**

**9.1 Assistance with Consumer Requests.** Vendor shall assist Company in fulfilling its obligations to respond to Consumer rights requests under Applicable Data Protection Laws, including but not limited to requests to know, access, correct, delete, port, and opt out of the sale or sharing of Personal Information, as well as requests to limit the use and disclosure of sensitive personal information. Vendor shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational processes to enable Company to comply with such Consumer requests in a timely and efficient manner.

**9.2 Notification of Direct Consumer Requests.** Vendor shall promptly, and in no event later than five (5) business days after receipt, notify Company if Vendor receives a Consumer rights request directly from a Consumer relating to Personal Information Processed on behalf of Company. Vendor shall not independently respond to, fulfill, or deny any such Consumer request unless directed to do so by Company in writing. Vendor shall refer the Consumer to Company for handling of the request, unless Company instructs otherwise.

**9.3 Systems and Processes for Consumer Requests.** Vendor shall maintain systems and processes capable of identifying, locating, retrieving, and, where applicable, deleting or correcting Personal Information by Consumer, in order to enable Company to respond to Consumer rights requests in compliance with the timeframes established by Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall ensure that its systems are designed to facilitate compliance with Company\'s obligations to respond to Consumer requests within forty-five (45) calendar days of receipt (or such other period as may be specified by Applicable Data Protection Laws), taking into account any extensions permitted by law.

**9.4 Identity Verification.** Vendor shall implement reasonable measures to verify the identity of Consumers submitting rights requests, in coordination with Company and in accordance with Company\'s identity verification procedures. Vendor shall not fulfill any Consumer request unless the identity of the requesting Consumer has been verified to Company\'s reasonable satisfaction. Vendor shall cooperate with Company in implementing and refining identity verification processes as needed.

**9.5 No Additional Fees.** Vendor shall not charge Company additional fees, surcharges, or other costs for assistance with Consumer rights requests that are part of Vendor\'s ordinary-course obligations under Applicable Data Protection Laws and this DPA. The Parties acknowledge that Vendor\'s obligation to assist with Consumer rights requests is an integral component of the services provided under the Agreement and is included in the fees paid by Company under the Agreement.
**[Article 10 --- De-Identification Standards]{.underline}**

**10.1 De-Identification Requirements.** If Vendor de-identifies Personal Information as part of the services provided under the Agreement, Vendor shall ensure that the de-identification process meets all requirements of Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), and any other applicable statutory or regulatory definitions of de-identification, including the GLBA de-identification requirements where applicable. Vendor shall document its de-identification methodologies and make such documentation available to Company upon request.

**10.2 Technical Safeguards Against Re-Identification.** Vendor shall implement and maintain technical safeguards and business processes that are reasonably designed to prevent re-identification of De-Identified Data, including without limitation: (a) the removal or transformation of direct identifiers; (b) the suppression or generalization of quasi-identifiers to levels that prevent re-identification; (c) the application of appropriate statistical disclosure limitation techniques; and (d) access controls and use restrictions specific to De-Identified Data.

**10.3 Prohibition on Re-Identification.** Vendor shall not attempt to re-identify De-Identified Data, and shall contractually prohibit its Sub-Processors, employees, contractors, and agents from attempting to re-identify De-Identified Data. In the event that Vendor or any of its Sub-Processors, employees, contractors, or agents inadvertently re-identifies any De-Identified Data, Vendor shall: (a) immediately cease use of the re-identified data; (b) promptly notify Company; and (c) delete or re-de-identify the data in accordance with Company\'s instructions.

**10.4 Independent Verification.** Vendor shall subject any de-identification methodology to independent verification by a qualified professional (such as a statistician, data scientist, or privacy engineer with relevant expertise) before deploying such methodology in production. Vendor shall provide Company with a summary of the independent verification, including the methodology used, the conclusions reached, and any limitations identified, upon Company\'s request.

**10.5 Public Commitment.** Vendor shall make publicly available, such as in its privacy policy or on its website, a commitment to maintain and use De-Identified Data only in de-identified form and to not attempt to re-identify the data, as required by Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and any other Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall provide Company with a link to or copy of such public commitment upon request.

**10.6 Sub-Processor Obligations.** Any contractual obligations regarding De-Identified Data imposed on Sub-Processors engaged by Vendor shall be no less protective than those set forth in this Article 10. Vendor shall ensure that all Sub-Processors comply with the de-identification standards, technical safeguards, and prohibitions on re-identification set forth herein.
**[Article 11 --- Data Return and Deletion upon Termination]{.underline}**

**11.1 Data Return or Deletion.** Upon the expiration or termination of the Agreement (for any reason), or upon Company\'s earlier written request at any time during the term of the Agreement, Vendor shall, at Company\'s sole election, either: (a) return to Company all Personal Information in Vendor\'s possession or control, in a commonly used, structured, machine-readable format designated by Company, including all copies, backups, archives, and replications of Personal Information; or (b) securely delete and destroy all Personal Information in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, archives, and replications, using methods that render the Personal Information permanently unrecoverable. Company shall communicate its election to Vendor in writing.

**11.2 Timeframe for Return or Deletion.** Vendor shall complete the return or secure deletion and destruction of all Personal Information within thirty (30) days of receiving Company\'s instruction under Section 11.1. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to complete such return or deletion as promptly as practicable within such period. If Vendor requires additional time due to the volume or complexity of the data, Vendor shall notify Company in writing, specifying the additional time needed and the reasons therefor, and the Parties shall agree in writing on a revised timeline.

**11.3 Certification of Deletion or Return.** Upon completion of the return or deletion of Personal Information, Vendor shall provide Company with a written certification, signed by an authorized officer of Vendor, confirming that: (a) all Personal Information has been returned or deleted in accordance with Company\'s instructions and this DPA; (b) no copies, backups, archives, or replications of Personal Information remain in Vendor\'s possession or control, except as permitted under Section 11.4; and (c) Vendor has directed all Sub-Processors to comply with the data return and deletion obligations set forth in this Article. Vendor shall provide such certification within ten (10) business days of completing the return or deletion.

**11.4 Retention Exception.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, Vendor may retain Personal Information only to the extent that retention is required by Applicable Data Protection Laws, and only for the duration and purposes required by such laws. In the event Vendor retains any Personal Information pursuant to this Section 11.4, Vendor shall: (a) promptly notify Company in writing, identifying the specific Personal Information retained, the legal basis for retention, and the anticipated duration of retention; (b) continue to protect such retained Personal Information in accordance with the terms of this DPA; (c) limit Processing of such Personal Information to the purposes required by law; and (d) securely delete and destroy such Personal Information promptly upon the expiration of the applicable retention period.

**11.5 Sub-Processor Compliance.** Vendor shall ensure that all Sub-Processors comply with the data return and deletion obligations set forth in this Article 11. Vendor shall include in its Sub-Processor agreements provisions requiring Sub-Processors to return or delete Personal Information in accordance with Vendor\'s instructions, and Vendor shall obtain written certifications from Sub-Processors confirming compliance with such obligations.
**[Article 12 --- Audit and Inspection Rights]{.underline}**

**12.1 Information Availability.** Vendor shall make available to Company, upon reasonable request, all information reasonably necessary to demonstrate Vendor\'s compliance with this DPA and Applicable Data Protection Laws. Such information may include, without limitation, policies and procedures, training records, security assessment results, Data Breach records, Sub-Processor agreements, SOC 2 Type II reports, and other relevant documentation.

**12.2 Right to Conduct Audits.** Company, or its authorized third-party auditor (subject to reasonable confidentiality obligations acceptable to Vendor and not being a competitor of Vendor), shall have the right to conduct audits and inspections of Vendor\'s Processing activities, facilities, systems, and records related to the Processing of Personal Information under this DPA. Company shall provide Vendor with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any planned audit, specifying the scope, duration, and personnel involved. Vendor and Company shall cooperate in good faith to agree on the timing and logistics of any audit to minimize disruption to Vendor\'s operations.

**12.3 Frequency of Audits.** Audits may be conducted no more than once per calendar year, unless: (a) a Data Breach involving Company\'s Personal Information has occurred; (b) Company has reasonable grounds to believe that Vendor is materially non-compliant with this DPA or Applicable Data Protection Laws; or (c) an audit or investigation is required or requested by a regulatory authority with jurisdiction over Company or Vendor. In any of the circumstances described in clauses (a) through (c), Company may conduct additional audits as reasonably necessary, upon reasonable notice to Vendor, which notice may be shorter than the thirty (30) days specified in Section 12.2 in the case of urgent circumstances.

**12.4 Cooperation with Audits.** Vendor shall cooperate fully with all audits and inspections conducted under this Article, and shall provide Company and its authorized auditors with reasonable access to Vendor\'s relevant personnel, systems, facilities, documentation, and records. Vendor shall respond to all reasonable audit-related inquiries and requests for documentation within ten (10) business days of receipt, or such shorter period as may be reasonably necessary in the circumstances.

**12.5 Audit Costs.** Vendor shall bear its own internal costs of cooperating with audits conducted under this Article, including the costs of making personnel, systems, and documentation available to Company\'s auditors. 108: Section 4.8 — Audit Rights
109: Vendor shall maintain accurate books and records relating to overage calculations and API call volumes. Customer shall have the right, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice, no more than once per Contract Year, to audit or have an independent third-party auditor audit Vendor's relevant records to verify the accuracy of invoiced overages. If an audit reveals an overcharge exceeding five percent (5%) of the audited amount, Vendor shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit and promptly refund the overcharge.
110: ARTICLE 5 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
111: Section 5.1 — Vendor IP Ownership
112: As between the Parties, Vendor is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to: (a) the Platform (excluding Customer-Trained Adaptations); (b) the Base Model; (c) all Derivative Models (excluding Customer-Trained Adaptations); and (d) all improvements, enhancements, updates, upgrades, modifications, and derivative works of any of the foregoing (excluding Customer-Trained Adaptations), together with all Intellectual Property Rights therein and thereto, regardless of whether such items are created by Vendor independently, in collaboration with Customer, or through the processing of Customer Data.
113: Section 5.2 — Customer Ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations
114: As between the Parties, Customer is and shall the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to all Customer-Trained Adaptations, including all fine-tuned weights, adapter layers, LoRA matrices, and any other model parameters generated through fine-tuning of the Base Model using Customer Data, together with all Intellectual Property Rights therein. Vendor hereby assigns and agrees to assign to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to such Customer-Trained Adaptations, effective upon creation. Vendor shall execute all documents and take all actions reasonably requested by Customer to evidence or perfect Customer's ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations.
115: Vendor is granted a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Customer-Trained Adaptations solely to the extent necessary to provide the Platform and perform its obligations under this Agreement during the Term. Such license shall automatically terminate upon expiration or termination of this Agreement.
116: Section 5.3 — Customer Data Ownership
117: As between the Parties, Customer is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to all Customer Data, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. Vendor's right to access, use, and process Customer Data is strictly limited to providing the Platform and performing its obligations under this Agreement as a service provider, and for no other purpose. Vendor shall not use Customer Data to train, improve, benchmark, or develop models, products, or services for any other customer or third party. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as transferring ownership of Customer Data from Customer to Vendor. Vendor acknowledges that Customer Data may contain NPPI and other regulated data, and Vendor agrees to treat all Customer Data in accordance with its obligations under this Agreement and applicable law.
118: Section 5. 4 — Feedback
119: If Customer or any of its employees, contractors, or agents provides any suggestions, enhancement requests, ideas, recommendations, corrections, or other feedback regarding the Platform, the Documentation, or any of Vendor's products or services (collectively, "Feedback"), Customer hereby grants to Vendor a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, transferable, sublicensable license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, create derivative works from, distribute, display, perform, and otherwise exploit such Feedback in any manner and for any purpose, without restriction, attribution, or compensation to Customer. Customer acknowledges that Vendor may use Feedback to improve the Platform, develop new features, or create new products or services, and that Vendor shall have no obligation to implement or incorporate any Feedback.
120: Section 5. 5 — No Other Rights
121: Except as expressly set forth in this Article 5 and the license granted in Section 2.1, neither Party grants the other Party any right, title, or interest in or to its Intellectual Property Rights, whether by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any rights in Vendor's trade secrets, proprietary algorithms, model architectures, training methodologies, or other confidential technical information, except as expressly provided herein.
122: ## ARTICLE 5A — TECHNOLOGY ESCROW
123: Section 5A.1 — Escrow Arrangement
124: Within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date, Vendor shall enter into a three-party escrow agreement with Customer and Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. (the "Escrow Agent"), in a form reasonably satisfactory to Customer, pursuant to which Vendor shall deposit the Escrow Materials.
125: Section 5A.2 — Escrow Deposits
126: Vendor shall deposit and maintain current versions of the following Escrow Materials:
127: (a) Complete source code for the Base Model, including all build scripts, compilers, and tools necessary to compile and deploy the Base Model;
128: (b) All Customer-Trained Adaptations, including fine-tuned adapter weights, training configuration files, and pipeline artifacts;
129: (c) All Documentation necessary to build, deploy, and operate the Platform;
130: (d) Complete dependency list, third-party library inventory, and license information.
131: Vendor shall update the Escrow Materials within thirty (30) days following any material update to the deposited materials, and in any event no less frequently than quarterly.
132: Section 5A.3 — Release Conditions
133: The Escrow Agent shall release the Escrow Materials to Customer upon the occurrence of any of the following release conditions:
134: (a) Vendor becomes the subject of a voluntary or involuntary petition in bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, liquidation, or similar proceeding, or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors;
135: (b) Vendor commits a material breach of this Agreement that remains uncured for more than sixty (60) days after Customer's written notice specifying the breach;
136: (c) Vendor ceases to support, maintain, or make available the Platform commercially, or publicly announces its intention to do so.
137: Upon release, Customer shall receive a non-exclusive, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license to use, modify, compile, and deploy the Escrow Materials solely for Customer's internal business purposes in connection with LendStream.
138: Section 5A.4 — Escrow Costs
139: Vendor shall bear all costs associated with establishing and maintaining the escrow arrangement, including Escrow Agent fees and deposit verification costs.
140: Section 5A.5 — Verification
141: Customer shall have the right, no more than once per Contract Year, to request verification by the Escrow Agent or a mutually agreed third-party technical expert that the Escrow Materials are complete, current, and sufficient to build and deploy the Platform. Vendor shall cooperate with such verification. The cost of verification shall be borne by Customer, unless verification reveals a material deficiency, in which case Vendor shall bear the cost.
142: ARTICLE 6 — DATA PROCESSING AND PRIVACY
143: Section 6.1 — Customer Data Processing
144: Vendor shall process Customer Data solely for the purpose of providing the Platform and performing Vendor's obligations under this Agreement. Vendor shall not process Customer Data for any other purpose, including without limitation training, improving, or benchmarking the Base Model or any Derivative Models for the benefit of Vendor or any third party. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data to any third party.
145: Section 6.2 — Service Provider / Processor Status
146: Vendor shall process Customer Data solely as a service provider (as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag)) and processor on behalf of Customer. Vendor shall not be deemed an independent controller with respect to any processing of Customer Data. Vendor shall certify its status as a service provider under the CCPA/CPRA in the Data Processing Addendum (Exhibit D).
147: Section 6.3 — Compliance with Laws
148: Each Party shall comply with all applicable data protection and privacy laws, rules, and regulations in connection with its processing of Customer Data under this Agreement, including without limitation: (a) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 6801–6809, and its implementing regulations, including Regulation S-P (17 C.F.R. Part 248) and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) ("GLBA"), to the extent applicable to the processing of NPPI; (b) the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.100–1798.199.100 ("CCPA/CPRA"), to the extent applicable; and (c) any other applicable federal, state, or international data protection or privacy laws. Vendor's obligations as a service provider under CCPA/CPRA are further set forth in the Data Processing Addendum (Exhibit D).
149: Section 6.4 — Security Measures
150: Vendor shall implement and maintain throughout the Term administrative, technical, and physical safeguards that are no less protective than industry-standard measures, including SOC 2 Type II controls, designed to protect Customer Data against unauthorized access, acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor's security program shall include: (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or equivalent); (b) access controls, including multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and least-privilege principles; (c) regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing; (d) intrusion detection and prevention systems; (e) security incident response procedures; and (f) employee security awareness training. Vendor shall, upon Customer's reasonable request and no more than once per twelve (12)-month period, provide Customer with a summary of Vendor's then-current security measures and any SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit reports covering Vendor's information security controls.
151: Section 6.5 — Data Breach Notification
152: In the event of any confirmed or reasonably suspected security breach involving the unauthorized access, acquisition, use, or disclosure of Customer Data (a "Security Breach"), Vendor shall: (a) notify Customer of the Security Breach within seventy-two (72) hours of discovery of the Security Breach; (b) promptly investigate the Security Breach and take reasonable steps to contain, mitigate, and remediate the Security Breach; (c) provide Customer with reasonably detailed information regarding the nature and scope of the Security Breach, including the categories and approximate number of data subjects affected, the measures taken or proposed to address the Security Breach, and the identity and contact information of Vendor's data protection officer or other contact point; and (d) cooperate with Customer in Customer's investigation, response, and notification obligations in connection with the Security Breach. The obligations set forth in this Section 6.5 shall not be construed as an acknowledgment by Vendor of any fault or liability with respect to the Security Breach.
153: Section 6.6 — Sub-Processors
154: Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer's prior written consent. Vendor shall maintain a list of sub-processors and provide such list to Customer upon request. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement and the DPA. Vendor shall remain fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.
155: Section 6. 7 — Return and Deletion of Data
156: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer's written election made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration, either (a) return Customer Data to Customer in a commercially reasonable format designated by Customer, or (b) securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor's possession or control, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof. Vendor shall complete such return or deletion within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of Customer's written request. Upon completion of the return or deletion, Vendor shall certify in writing to Customer that all Customer Data has been returned or deleted in accordance with this Section 6. 7. Vendor shall not retain any Customer Data in any form following termination, except as required by applicable law, in which case Vendor shall (i) isolate such data, (ii) continue to protect it in accordance with this Agreement, and (iii) delete it as soon as the retention obligation expires. For the avoidance of doubt, no exception shall apply for de-identified or aggregated data, which shall also be returned or deleted upon Customer's request.

191: ARTICLE 9 — SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS
192: Section 9.1 — Uptime
193: Vendor shall maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the "Uptime SLA"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
194: Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100
195: For purposes of the Uptime SLA, "Downtime" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor's monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer's systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer's acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer's access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).
196: Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours' advance written notice to Customer's designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
197: Section 9.2 — Latency
198: Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor's internal monitoring systems at the Platform's API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor's receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor's transmission of the corresponding API response.
199: Section 9.3 — Model Accuracy
200: Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer's production document processing workloads.
201: During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.
202: Section 9.4 — Service Credits
203: In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a "Service Credit"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred.
204: Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer's next invoice(s) under this Agreement . If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed thirty percent (30%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. Service Credits are not Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5.
205: Section 9.5 — Termination for Chronic SLA Failure
206: If Vendor fails to meet any SLA target (Uptime, Latency, or Accuracy) for three (3) or more consecutive calendar months, Customer shall have the right to terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days' written notice, without payment of any early termination fee, and Vendor shall refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Annual Platform Fees for the period following the effective date of termination.
207: Section 9. 6 — Reporting
208: Vendor shall provide Customer with monthly reports in a machine-readable format detailing Platform uptime, API latency, and model accuracy metrics for the preceding calendar month. Such reports shall be delivered to Customer within five (5) business days following the end of each calendar month. Reports shall include, at a minimum: (a) Platform availability percentage; (b) total Downtime minutes and the cause of each incident; (c) API latency at the 50th percentile (p50) , 95th percentile (p95), and 99th percentile (p99); (d) model accuracy metrics, including F1 score, precision, and recall, as measured against the validation dataset; and (e) API call usage data, including the total number of API calls consumed during the month and the cumulative total for the current Contract Year. Customer shall have the right to independently verify reported metrics against its own monitoring data. Vendor shall make authorized Customer personnel available for a monthly service review meeting, upon Customer's reasonable request, to discuss the monthly reports and any performance issues.

211: IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF GOODWILL, LOSS OF DATA, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES, COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES, BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, OR ANY OTHER COMMERCIAL DAMAGES OR LOSSES, WHETHER ARISING UNDER CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES OR COULD HAVE FORESEEN SUCH DAMAGES. **Calculating credit cap**

I'm thinking about Exhibit B's current uptime tier, which is at 30%. I should cap it at 20% and below 99.50, which would mean a 20% credit cap of the monthly fees at $40,000. The instruction specifically asks me to propose this cap based on the fees, so this seems to align well. It feels straightforward, but I'll double-check that this reflects the intended guidelines before finalizing.

**Refining accuracy measurements**

I'm considering adjustments to the full schedule to potentially preserve levels, but capping at 20%. I think I need to format this in a table rather than paragraphs, likely focusing on single cell paragraphs with exact text. I could also revise the document XML by changing all occurrences of `30% ($60,000)` to `20% ($40,000)` using tracked changes.

Regarding the latency threshold, I might change from 400 to 450 while ensuring the accuracy remains at 0.94 for two consecutive quarterly measurements. I'll need to confirm if adjustments to monthly measurements are necessary. It seems there's an unclear link between Exhibit B and accuracy measurements, especially with potential service credits for below-target F1 scores.

**Aligning liability and confidentiality**

I want to ensure everything aligns without introducing inconsistencies, particularly around the 20% cap.

The termination trigger is currently set at three consecutive months, which is good. Uptime is at 99.95%, and that’s not changing. For liability under Section 10.2, I need to adjust it from 2x $4.8 to 1.5x $3.6. 

Section 10.3 touches on IP indemnity and data breaches, which are currently uncapped. I think I should introduce a super-cap of 3x $7.2 there, while willful misconduct and gross negligence remain uncapped. Regarding confidentiality, it seems we could keep it uncapped as the playbook suggests this as a preferred option. I need to modify Section 10.3 to define super-cap and clarify its application.

**Clarifying indemnity provisions**

I want to ensure that AI-output indemnity is correctly categorized, possibly under IP or legal obligations. If it's a new provision, it should probably fall under either a super-cap or a general cap.

Draft instructions support the idea of a super-cap for IP indemnity obligations and data breach carve-outs, so it makes sense that new AI-output indemnity claims would also be subject to that. I think I should add a note stating it’s "Subject to Section 10.3" to clarify its standing.

**Rephrasing IP Rights Section**

I need to replace the second paragraph of Section 11.1 to explicitly state “all IP rights including…analogous foreign laws.” It seems like we should remove any limitations related to registration as it’s already broad. I want to ensure that this section covers everything necessary without being overly restrictive. It’s important that the wording is clear to avoid any misunderstandings. I'll make these changes to align the language properly!

**Planning document revisions**

I need to include the actual tracked changes in the output based on the accepted draft. We should set the revision author's name to "Kirkstead & Yao" with a date of 2025-05-14 and update change IDs. It seems like I'll need to write a script to parse the normalized docx first, then modify all occurrences in the relevant paragraphs using content replacements. I also need to handle clause 5.2, which spans two paragraphs, replacing p114 with a new full paragraph and p115 with a new second paragraph that has a non-assertion.

    return r

def revision(tag,text,cid):
    el=etree.Element(q(tag), {q('id'):str(cid), q('author'):REV_AUTHOR, q('date'):REV_DATE})
    el.append(make_run(text, deleted=(tag=='del')))
    return el

def replace_p(p,new,cid,old=None):
    oldtxt=old if old is not None else p_text(p)
    ppr=p.find(q('pPr'))
    for child in list(p):
        if child is not ppr: p.remove(child)
    if oldtxt:
        p.append(revision('del',oldtxt,cid)); cid+=1
    p.append(revision('ins',new,cid))
    return cid+1

def insert_after(p,text,cid):
    np=etree.Element(q('p'))
    ppr=p.find(q('pPr'))
    if ppr is not None: np.append(copy.deepcopy(ppr))
    np.append(revision('ins',text,cid))
    p.getparent().insert(p.getparent().index(p)+1,np)
    return np,cid+1

def all_ps(root): return root.xpath('.//w:body//w:p',namespaces=ns)

def find_p(root, needle, occurrence=0):
    hits=[p for p in all_ps(root) if needle in p_text(p)]
    if len(hits)<=occurrence:
        raise ValueError(f'not found {needle!r}; got {len(hits)}')
    return hits[occurrence]

def replace_containing(root, needle, new, cid, occurrence=0):
    p=find_p(root,needle,occurrence)
    return replace_p(p,new,cid)

def set_track_revisions(data):
    root=etree.fromstring(data); settings=root
    if not settings.xpath('.//w:trackRevisions',namespaces=ns): settings.append(etree.Element(q('trackRevisions')))
    return etree.tostring(settings,xml_declaration=True,encoding='UTF-8',standalone=True)

AI PLATFORM AGREEMENT
This AI Platform Agreement (this \"Agreement\"), dated as of April 2, 2025, is entered into by and between:
TechNova Solutions, Inc., a Delaware corporation, with its principal offices located at 4200 Ridgeline Parkway, Suite 1100, Austin, TX 78735 (\"Customer\"),
and
Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, with its principal offices located at 75 Federal Street, 14th Floor, Boston, MA 02110 (\"Vendor\").
Vendor and Customer are each referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"
RECITALS

WHEREAS, Vendor has developed and operates a proprietary large-language-model-based document processing platform known as MeridianIQ (the \"Platform\"), which leverages advanced artificial intelligence and natural language processing capabilities to facilitate automated document processing, analysis, and classification;

WHEREAS, Customer desires to license access to the Platform on a software-as-a-service basis for use in connection with Customer\'s lending technology product known as LendStream, and Vendor desires to provide such access, subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein;

WHEREAS, Customer and Vendor desire to set forth the terms and conditions under which Vendor will provide Customer with access to the Platform, including the scope of the license grant, implementation and fine-tuning services, service level commitments, intellectual property ownership, data processing obligations, and related commercial terms; and

WHEREAS, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements hereinafter set forth and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

ARTICLE 1 --- DEFINITIONS

As used in this Agreement, the following capitalized terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used in this Agreement that are not defined in this Article 1 shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

ARTICLE 2 --- LICENSE GRANT AND SCOPE OF USE
Section 2.1 --- License Grant

Customer shall be responsible for all acts and omissions of its employees and authorized contractors in connection with their access to and use of the Platform. Use of the Platform is limited to the processing, analysis, and classification of Customer Data in support of LendStream\'s document processing workflows. ARTICLE 3 --- IMPLEMENTATION AND TRAINING SERVICES

301: Section 6.6 --- Sub-Processors
302: 
303: Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall maintain a list of sub-processors and provide such list to Customer upon request. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement and the DPA. Vendor shall remain fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.
304: 
305: Section 6. 7 --- Return and Deletion of Data
306: 
307: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer\'s written election made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration, either (a) return Customer Data to Customer in a commercially reasonable format designated by Customer, or (b) securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof. Vendor shall complete such return or deletion within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of Customer\'s written request. Upon completion of the return or deletion, Vendor shall certify in writing to Customer that all Customer Data has been returned or deleted in accordance with this Section 6. 7. Vendor shall not retain any Customer Data in any form following termination, except as required by applicable law, in which case Vendor shall (i) isolate such data, (ii) continue to protect it in accordance with this Agreement, and (iii) delete it as soon as the retention obligation expires. For the avoidance of doubt, no exception shall apply for de-identified or aggregated data, which shall also be returned or deleted upon Customer\'s request.
308: 
309: Section 6.8 --- Data Processing Addendum
310: 
311: The Parties shall execute the Data Processing Addendum attached as Exhibit D contemporaneously with this Agreement. The DPA is incorporated into and forms part of this Agreement. In the event of any conflict between the DPA and this Agreement, the DPA shall control with respect to data protection matters.

313: ARTICLE 7 --- CONFIDENTIALITY
314: 
315: Section 7.1 --- Definition of Confidential Information
316: 
317: \"Confidential Information\" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the \"Disclosing Party\") to the other Party (the \"Receiving Party\") in connection with this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, and whether or not marked or designated as \"confidential,\" \"proprietary,\" or with any similar legend, that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Confidential Information includes: (a) business plans, strategies, forecasts, and financial information; (b) technical information, including source code, algorithms, model architectures, model weights, training data, APIs, and system designs; (c) trade secrets; (d) customer lists, supplier lists, and pricing information; (e) product roadmaps and development plans; and (f) the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including all pricing, fee, and commercial terms. Customer Data shall be deemed Confidential Information of Customer regardless of whether it is marked or designated as confidential.
318: 
319: Confidential Information shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or breach by the Receiving Party; (ii) was already known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records; (iii) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality owed to the Disclosing Party; or (iv) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records.
320: 
321: Section 7.2 --- Obligations
322: 
323: The Receiving Party shall: (a) hold the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) not disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted under Section 7.3; (c) use the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement; and (d) protect the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information using measures that are no less protective than those used by the Receiving Party to protect its own most sensitive confidential information, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.
324: 
325: The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 7 shall remain in effect during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the date of disclosure; provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.
326: 
327: Section 7.3 --- Permitted Disclosures
328: 
329: The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, advisors, and Affiliates who have a legitimate need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 7 (collectively, \"Authorized Recipients\"). The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 7 by its Authorized Recipients.
330: 
331: The Receiving Party may also disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal process, provided that the Receiving Party: (a) provides the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permitted) so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party\'s expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) discloses only the minimum amount of Confidential Information necessary to comply with such requirement. Any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to a legal compulsion shall retain its confidential status for all other purposes under this Agreement.
332: 
333: Section 7.4 --- Injunctive Relief
334: 
335: Each Party acknowledges that a breach of this Article 7 may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, each Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting a bond or other security.

377: ARTICLE 9 --- SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS
378: 
379: Section 9.1 --- Uptime
380: 
381: Vendor shall maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the \"Uptime SLA\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
382: 
383: > Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100
384: 
385: For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"Downtime\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).
386: 
387: Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice to Customer\'s designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
388: 
389: Section 9.2 --- Latency (p95 ≤ 450 ms)
390: 
391: Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 450 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred fifty (450) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 450 ms) during each calendar month, as measured at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.

393: Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy
394: 
395: Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score against the mutually agreed validation dataset and methodology documented in the applicable Statement of Work, at or above F1 ≥ 0.92 throughout the ninety (90)-day Stabilization Period following Go-Live (October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025), and at or above F1 ≥ 0.94 beginning January 1, 2026. The Parties shall review the validation dataset and methodology no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure that they remain representative of Customer\'s production workloads.
396: 
397: During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.92, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.During the Stabilization Period (October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025), the contractual Model Accuracy target is F1 ≥ 0.92. Beginning January 1, 2026, the contractual target is F1 ≥ 0.94.During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.92, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.During the Stabilization Period (October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025), the contractual Model Accuracy target is F1 ≥ 0.92. Beginning January 1, 2026, the contractual target is F1 ≥ 0.94.
