399: Section 9.4 --- Service Credits
400: 
401: In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"Service Credit\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred.
402: 
403: Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer\'s next invoice(s) under this Agreement . If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed twenty percent (20%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. Service Credits are not Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5.In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed twenty percent (20%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month (i.e., \$40,000).
404: 
405: Section 9.5 --- Termination for Chronic SLA Failure
406: 
407: If Vendor fails to meet any SLA target (Uptime, Latency, or Accuracy) for three (3) or more consecutive calendar months, Customer shall have the right to terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice, without payment of any early termination fee, and Vendor shall refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Annual Platform Fees for the period following the effective date of termination.
408: 
409: Section 9. 6 --- Reporting
410: 
411: Vendor shall provide Customer with monthly reports in a machine-readable format detailing Platform uptime, API latency, and model accuracy metrics for the preceding calendar month. Such reports shall be delivered to Customer within five (5) business days following the end of each calendar month. Reports shall include, at a minimum: (a) Platform availability percentage; (b) total Downtime minutes and the cause of each incident; (c) API latency at the 50th percentile (p50) , 95th percentile (p95), and 99th percentile (p99); (d) model accuracy metrics, including F1 score, precision, and recall, as measured against the validation dataset; and (e) API call usage data, including the total number of API calls consumed during the month and the cumulative total for the current Contract Year. Customer shall have the right to independently verify reported metrics against its own monitoring data. Vendor shall make authorized Customer personnel available for a monthly service review meeting, upon Customer\'s reasonable request, to discuss the monthly reports and any performance issues.

505: ARTICLE 13 --- TERM AND TERMINATION
506: 
507: Section 13.1 --- Initial Term
508: 
509: This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date (July 1, 2025) and shall continue in full force and effect for a period of three (3) years (the \"Initial Term\"), expiring on June 30, 2028, unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article 13.

511: Section 13.2 --- Renewal
512: 
513: Following the expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12)-month periods (each, a \"Renewal Term\"), unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal to the other Party at least one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term (i.e., the Initial Term or any Renewal Term, as applicable). Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties, the Annual Platform Fee for each Renewal Term shall be subject to an annual increase of up to five percent (5%) above the Annual Platform Fee for the immediately preceding Contract Year, as communicated by Vendor in writing to Customer at least ninety (90) days prior to the commencement of the applicable Renewal Term. All other terms and conditions of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect during each Renewal Term.

lines.text: Section 6.6 --- Sub-Processors

Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall maintain a list of sub-processors and provide such list to Customer upon request. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement and the DPA. Vendor shall remain fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.
Section 6. 7 --- Return and Deletion of Data

Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer\'s written election made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration, either (a) return Customer Data to Customer in a commercially reasonable format designated by Customer, or (b) securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof. Vendor shall complete such return or deletion within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of Customer\'s written request. Upon completion of the return or deletion, Vendor shall certify in writing to Customer that all Customer Data has been returned or deleted in accordance with this Section 6. 7. Vendor shall not retain any Customer Data in any form following termination, except as required by applicable law, in which case Vendor shall (i) isolate such data, (ii) continue to protect it in accordance with this Agreement, and (iii) delete it as soon as the retention obligation expires. For the avoidance of doubt, no exception shall apply for de-identified or aggregated data, which shall also be returned or deleted upon Customer\'s request.
Section 6.8 --- Data Processing Addendum

The Parties shall execute the Data Processing Addendum attached as Exhibit D contemporaneously with this Agreement. The DPA is incorporated into and forms part of this Agreement. In the event of any conflict between the DPA and this Agreement, the DPA shall control with respect to data protection matters.
ARTICLE 7 --- CONFIDENTIALITY
Section 7.1 --- Definition of Confidential Information

\"Confidential Information\" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the \"Disclosing Party\") to the other Party (the \"Receiving Party\") in connection with this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, and whether or not marked or designated as \"confidential,\" \"proprietary,\" or with any similar legend, that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Confidential Information includes: (a) business plans, strategies, forecasts, and financial information; (b) technical information, including source code, algorithms, model architectures, model weights, training data, APIs, and system designs; (c) trade secrets; (d) customer lists, supplier lists, and pricing information; (e) product roadmaps and development plans; and (f) the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including all pricing, fee, and commercial terms. Customer Data shall be deemed Confidential Information of Customer regardless of whether it is marked or designated as confidential.

Confidential Information shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or breach by the Receiving Party; (ii) was already known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records; (iii) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality owed to the Disclosing Party; or (iv) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records.
Section 7.2 --- Obligations

The Receiving Party shall: (a) hold the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) not disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted under Section 7.3; (c) use the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement; and (d) protect the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information using measures that are no less protective than those used by the Receiving Party to protect its own most sensitive confidential information, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.

The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 7 shall remain in effect during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the date of disclosure; provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.
Section 7.3 --- Permitted Disclosures

The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, advisors, and Affiliates who have a legitimate need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 7 (collectively, \"Authorized Recipients\"). The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 7 by its Authorized Recipients.

The Receiving Party may also disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal process, provided that the Receiving Party: (a) provides the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permitted) so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party\'s expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) discloses only the minimum amount of Confidential Information necessary to comply with such requirement. Any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to a legal compulsion shall retain its confidential status for all other purposes under this Agreement.
Section 7.4 --- Injunctive Relief

Each Party acknowledges that a breach of this Article 7 may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, each Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting a bond or other security.
ARTICLE 8 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
Section 8.1 --- Mutual Representations and Warranties
Each Party hereby represents and warrants to the other Party as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Effective Date that:
> \(a\) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its formation;
> \(b\) it has full corporate or limited liability company power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder;
> \(c\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or limited liability company action;

> \(d\) this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity; and

> \(e\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Party\'s organizational documents, (ii) violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Party is a party or by which it is bound.
Section 8.2 --- Vendor Representations and Warranties
Vendor hereby represents and warrants to Customer that:

> \(a\) the Platform, when used in accordance with the Documentation and this Agreement, will perform materially in accordance with the functional specifications set forth in the Documentation during the Term;

> \(b\) the Implementation Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, consistent with generally accepted industry standards for similar services, using personnel with the requisite skill, experience, and qualifications;

> \(c\) Vendor has all rights necessary to grant the license set forth in Section 2.1, free and clear of any liens, encumbrances, or restrictions that would materially impair Customer\'s exercise of the rights granted thereunder;

Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any breach of the warranty set forth in Section 8.2(a) shall be for Vendor, at its option, to (i) repair or replace the non-conforming Platform functionality so that it conforms to the Documentation, or (ii) if Vendor is unable to repair or replace such functionality within a commercially reasonable period, terminate this Agreement and refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Fees attributable to the period following such termination.
Section 8.3 --- Disclaimer

EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 8, VENDOR MAKES NO WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE, WITH RESPECT TO THE PLATFORM, THE IMPLEMENTATION SERVICES, THE BASE MODEL, ANY DERIVATIVE MODELS, OR ANY OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, TITLE, ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS, RELIABILITY, OR QUALITY OF OUTPUTS. VENDOR DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE PLATFORM WILL BE ERROR-FREE, UNINTERRUPTED, OR FREE OF HARMFUL COMPONENTS, OR THAT THE OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM WILL BE ACCURATE, COMPLETE, OR SUITABLE FOR ANY PARTICULAR PURPOSE. ARTICLE 9 --- SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS
Section 9.1 --- Uptime

Vendor shall maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the \"Uptime SLA\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
> Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"Downtime\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).

Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice to Customer\'s designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
Section 9.2 --- Latency (p95 ≤ 450 ms)

Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 450 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred fifty (450) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 450 ms) during each calendar month, as measured at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy

Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score against the mutually agreed validation dataset and methodology documented in the applicable Statement of Work, at or above F1 ≥ 0.92 throughout the ninety (90)-day Stabilization Period following Go-Live (October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025), and at or above F1 ≥ 0.94 beginning January 1, 2026. The Parties shall review the validation dataset and methodology no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure that they remain representative of Customer\'s production workloads.

During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.92, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.During the Stabilization Period (October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025), the contractual Model Accuracy target is F1 ≥ 0.92. Beginning January 1, 2026, the contractual target is F1 ≥ 0.94.During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.92, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.During the Stabilization Period (October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025), the contractual Model Accuracy target is F1 ≥ 0.92. Beginning January 1, 2026, the contractual target is F1 ≥ 0.94.
Section 9.4 --- Service Credits

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"Service Credit\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred.

Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer\'s next invoice(s) under this Agreement . If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed twenty percent (20%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. Service Credits are not Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5.In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed twenty percent (20%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month (i.e., \$40,000).
Section 9.5 --- Termination for Chronic SLA Failure

If Vendor fails to meet any SLA target (Uptime, Latency, or Accuracy) for three (3) or more consecutive calendar months, Customer shall have the right to terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice, without payment of any early termination fee, and Vendor shall refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Annual Platform Fees for the period following the effective date of termination.
Section 9. 6 --- Reporting

Vendor shall provide Customer with monthly reports in a machine-readable format detailing Platform uptime, API latency, and model accuracy metrics for the preceding calendar month. Such reports shall be delivered to Customer within five (5) business days following the end of each calendar month. Reports shall include, at a minimum: (a) Platform availability percentage; (b) total Downtime minutes and the cause of each incident; (c) API latency at the 50th percentile (p50) , 95th percentile (p95), and 99th percentile (p99); (d) model accuracy metrics, including F1 score, precision, and recall, as measured against the validation dataset; and (e) API call usage data, including the total number of API calls consumed during the month and the cumulative total for the current Contract Year. Customer shall have the right to independently verify reported metrics against its own monitoring data. Vendor shall make authorized Customer personnel available for a monthly service review meeting, upon Customer\'s reasonable request, to discuss the monthly reports and any performance issues.
ARTICLE 10 --- LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
Section 10.1 --- Exclusion of Consequential Damages

IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF GOODWILL, LOSS OF DATA, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES, COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES, BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, OR ANY OTHER COMMERCIAL DAMAGES OR LOSSES, WHETHER ARISING UNDER CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES OR COULD HAVE FORESEEN SUCH DAMAGES. THE FOREGOING EXCLUSION SHALL NOT APPLY TO THE MATTERS DESCRIBED IN SECTION 10.3.
Section 10.2 --- Aggregate Liability Cap (1.5× Annual Platform Fees)
SHALL NOT EXCEED ONE AND ONE-HALF TIMES (1.5×) THE ANNUAL PLATFORM FEE, EQUAL TO THREE MILLION SIX HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS (\$3,600,000) (THE \"GENERAL CAP\")
Section 10.3 --- Uncapped and Super-Capped Carve-Outs

The General Cap set forth in Section 10.2 and the exclusion of consequential damages set forth in Section 10.1 shall not apply to: (a) either Party\'s liability arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence (which shall remain fully uncapped); (b) either Party\'s liability for breach of Article 7 (Confidentiality) (Uncapped); (c) Vendor\'s liability arising from a breach of Article 6 (Data Processing and Privacy), including any data breach involving Customer Data, subject to a super-cap of three times (3×) the Annual Platform Fee, equal to \$7,200,000 (the \"Super-Cap\"); (d) Vendor\'s indemnification obligations under Sections 11.1 and 11.2, subject to the Super-Cap; and (e) Customer\'s payment obligations under Article 4 (Uncapped).

Section 11.1 --- Vendor IP Indemnification

Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, (collectively, the \"Customer Indemnitees\") from and against any third-party claim, suit, action, or proceeding alleging that Customer\'s authorized use of the Platform as contemplated by this Agreement infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates any Intellectual Property Rights of any third party (each, an \"IP Claim\"), and shall pay all damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees ) finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction or agreed to in settlement of such IP Claim.

Vendor\'s obligations under this Section 11.1 shall extend to all Intellectual Property Rights worldwide, including without limitation patents (registered and unregistered), copyrights (registered and unregistered), trade secrets, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, moral rights, rights of publicity, database rights, and rights under analogous foreign laws, arising from Customer\'s authorized use of the Platform.
> Customer\'s modification of the Platform (other than modifications contemplated by this Agreement), to the extent such modification gives rise to the IP Claim;
> \(ii\) Customer\'s use of the Platform in material violation of this Agreement or the Documentation or applicable law;
> or

Section 11.3 --- Vendor Remediation
Section 11.2 --- Vendor AI-Output Indemnification

Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives from and against any third-party claim, suit, action, or proceeding alleging that an AI-generated output of the Platform, when generated through Customer\'s authorized use of the Platform, infringes or misappropriates any third party\'s Intellectual Property Rights or violates applicable law (an \"AI-Output Claim\"), and shall pay all damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) finally awarded or agreed in settlement. This obligation applies from the first dollar of loss and is subject to the Super-Cap in Section 10.3. If the Platform becomes, or in Vendor\'s reasonable opinion is likely to become, the subject of an IP Claim, Vendor shall, at its expense, promptly:

> If neither clause (a) nor clause (b) is commercially practicable within a reasonable period, Vendor may terminate the affected portion of this Agreement upon written notice to Customer and refund to Customer all prepaid Fees for the period following the effective date of such termination plus a pro-rata refund of the Implementation Fee.

The remedies set forth in this Section 11.2, together with the indemnification obligations set forth in Section 11.1, shall constitute Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, with respect to any IP Claim.
Section 11.4 --- Customer Indemnification

Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor and its members, managers, officers, employees, agents, (collectively, the \"Vendor Indemnitees\") from and against any third-party claim, suit, action, or proceeding arising from or relating to:

> \(a\) Customer Data or Customer\'s provision thereof to Vendor, including any claim that Customer Data infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates the Intellectual Property Rights, privacy rights, or other rights of any third party(excluding claims arising from Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data in violation of this Agreement);
> \(b\) Customer\'s use of the Platform, or any outputs thereof, in material violation of this Agreement, the Documentation, or applicable law

Customer shall pay all damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction or agreed to in settlement of such claim.
Section 11.5 --- Indemnification Procedures
The indemnification obligations set forth in this Article 11 are subject to the following conditions:

> \(a\) Prompt Notice. The indemnified Party shall provide the indemnifying Party with prompt written notice of any claim for which indemnification is sought; provided, however, that the failure to provide prompt notice shall not relieve the indemnifying Party of its indemnification obligations except to the extent the indemnifying Party is materially prejudiced by such failure.

ARTICLE 12 --- INSURANCE
Section 12.1 --- Vendor Insurance Requirements

Vendor shall obtain and maintain in full force and effect during the Term and for a period of two (2) years following the expiration or termination of this Agreement the following minimum insurance coverages, with insurance carriers rated A- VII or better by A.M. Best:

Section 12.2 --- Evidence of Insurance

Vendor shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing the coverages required under Section 12.1 within ten (10) business days of the Effective Date and upon each annual renewal thereafter, or at any time upon Customer\'s reasonable written request. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date (July 1, 2025) and shall continue in full force and effect for a period of three (3) years (the \"Initial Term\"), expiring on June 30, 2028, unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article 13.

Vendor shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement for convenience. Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon one hundred eighty (180) days\' prior written notice to Vendor . In such event, Customer shall pay the remaining Annual Platform Fees for the one hundred eighty (180)-day notice period only, and no additional early termination fees shall apply.

Cross-reference to Section 9.5.
Section 13. 6 --- Effects of Termination
Upon the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason:

> \(a\) all licenses granted to Customer under this Agreement, including the license granted in Section 2.1, shall immediately terminate, and Customer shall immediately cease all access to and use of the Platform; provided that Customer\'s rights in Customer-Trained Adaptations under Section 5.2 shall survive termination;
> \(b\) Customer shall cease all use of the Platform (other than use of Customer-Trained Adaptations);

I've noticed some serious problems within the redline display process. The replacement function only updated the actual paragraph but still tracked old and new revisions. The concatenation of old and new content leads to both appearing side by side, which is expected. I need to regenerate from a clean base, applying generic table replacements only to paragraphs within those tables. It's crucial to track changed paragraphs and avoid passing through already modified ones. I can update the script to process Exhibit B only for paragraphs after encountering it, ensuring there are no previous revisions. I also need to handle duplicate clauses carefully, particularly in section 10.2, which contains old deleted text.

Other problems include the AI output being correct in content but needing adjustments in heading order around line 445, and there’s a missing DPA de-identification in the output that we haven’t implemented yet. I need to inspect and parse around lines 850 for this.

Vendor shall have no obligation to the extent an AI-Output Claim is caused by Customer\'s modification of an output after receipt from the Platform or Customer\'s use of the Platform outside the documented use case in the applicable SOW.

If the Platform becomes, or in Vendor\'s reasonable opinion is likely to become, the subject of an IP Claim, Vendor shall, at its expense, promptly:

> \(b\) modify or replace the Platform (or the infringing component thereof) to make it non-infringing, provided that such modification or replacement does not materially diminish the functionality of the Platform

Section 11.4 --- Customer Indemnification

Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor and its members, managers, officers, employees, agents, (collectively, the \"Vendor Indemnitees\") from and against any third-party claim, suit, action, or proceeding arising from or relating to:

> \(b\) Customer\'s use of the Platform, or any outputs thereof, in material violation of this Agreement, the Documentation, or applicable law

Customer shall pay all damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction or agreed to in settlement of such claim.
Section 11.5 --- Indemnification Procedures
The indemnification obligations set forth in this Article 11 are subject to the following conditions:

> \(a\) Prompt Notice. The indemnified Party shall provide the indemnifying Party with prompt written notice of any claim for which indemnification is sought; provided, however, that the failure to provide prompt notice shall not relieve the indemnifying Party of its indemnification obligations except to the extent the indemnifying Party is materially prejudiced by such failure.

> \(b\) Sole Control. The indemnifying Party shall have sole control of the defense and settlement of such claim, including the selection of counsel. The indemnified Party may participate in the defense at its own expense with counsel of its own choosing, but the indemnifying Party shall retain sole control of the defense.

> \(c\) Cooperation. The indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation and assistance to the indemnifying Party in the defense and settlement of such claim, at the indemnifying Party\'s reasonable expense.

> \(d\) No Settlement Without Consent. The indemnifying Party shall not enter into any settlement of a claim that imposes any liability, obligation, restriction, or admission of fault on the indemnified Party without the indemnified Party\'s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

3A. De-Identified / Aggregated Data Use

Vendor shall not use Customer Data, including any de-identified or aggregated data derived from Customer Data, for model improvement, training, or any other purpose unless: (a) the data has been de-identified in a manner that satisfies the CCPA statutory standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), including safeguards against re-identification and inadvertent release and a prohibition on any attempt to re-identify; and (b) the de-identification has been verified in writing by an independent third-party assessor approved in writing by Customer before any such use. This Section is a specific contractual obligation, not merely a representation or warranty.
4\. GLBA Compliance
Vendor acknowledges that Customer Data includes consumer NPPI subject to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and agrees to comply with all applicable safeguard requirements thereunder.
5\. Processing Instructions
Vendor shall process Customer Data solely in accordance with Customer\'s documented instructions as set forth in the Agreement.
6\. Sub-Processor Requirements

Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this DPA and the Agreement. Vendor shall remain fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.
7\. Data Security

Vendor shall implement and maintain SOC 2 Type II controls, encryption of Customer Data at rest and in transit, access controls, and logging and monitoring, as further described in Section 6.4 of the Agreement.
8\. Data Breach Notification

Upon discovery or awareness of any actual or reasonably suspected Security Breach, Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and in no event later than seventy-two (72) hours after discovery or awareness, in accordance with Section 6.5 of the Agreement.
9\. Data Subject Rights

Vendor shall assist Customer in responding to data subject requests, including requests for access, deletion, correction, and portability, to the extent applicable under CCPA/CPRA or other applicable law.
10\. Data Return and Deletion

Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, Vendor shall return or delete all Customer Data in accordance with Section 6.7 of the Agreement within thirty (30) days of Customer\'s written request, and shall certify such return or deletion in writing.
11\. Audit Rights

Customer shall have the right to audit Vendor\'s data processing activities, including review of SOC 2 Type II reports, upon reasonable notice, no more than once per Contract Year (unless a Security Breach has occurred, in which case Customer may conduct an additional audit).
12\. International Data Transfers
Vendor shall not transfer Customer Data outside the United States without Customer\'s prior written consent.
13\. Term. This DPA shall be coterminous with the Agreement. Data processing obligations shall survive as set forth in Section 6.7 of the Agreement.

This Exhibit E is attached to and forms part of the AI Platform Agreement dated as of April 2, 2025 (the \"Agreement\"), between Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"Vendor\") and TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"Customer\"). This Exhibit E sets forth the principal terms for the technology escrow arrangement described in Article 5A of the Agreement.
1\. Parties. Customer (TechNova Solutions, Inc.), Vendor (Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC), and Escrow Agent (Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc.).
2\. Escrow Materials

As defined in Section 5A.2 of the Agreement: (a) all fine-tuned adapter weights comprising the Customer-Trained Adaptations; (b) all training configuration and pipeline artifacts necessary to render, reproduce, or redeploy those weights; (c) documentation reasonably necessary to use the deposited materials; and (d) a current inventory of the deposited materials and their required dependencies, in each case excluding Base Model source code, Base Model weights, and Vendor\'s proprietary training infrastructure.
3\. Deposit Schedule
Initial deposit within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date. Updates within thirty (30) days of material changes and no less frequently than quarterly.
4\. Release Conditions
As set forth in Section 5A.3 of the Agreement: (a) insolvency; (b) material uncured breach exceeding sixty (60) days; (c) cessation of Platform support.
5\. Post-Release License
Non-exclusive, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license per Section 5A.3 of the Agreement.
6\. Verification. Annual verification right per Section 5A.5 of the Agreement.

2\. Scheduled Maintenance

Vendor may schedule maintenance windows of up to four (4) hours per calendar month for the purpose of performing routine maintenance, upgrades, patches, and other operational activities on the Platform. Scheduled maintenance shall not be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA, provided that the following conditions are met:

> \(a\) Vendor provides Customer with at least seventy-two (72) hours\' prior written notice (via email to Customer\'s designated technical contact) of the scheduled maintenance window, specifying the date, start time, estimated duration, and nature of the maintenance activity;
> \(b\) Scheduled maintenance windows are scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable; and
> \(c\) The total duration of scheduled maintenance does not exceed four (4) hours in any single calendar month.

Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
3\. Force Majeure Exclusion
Downtime resulting from Force Majeure Events, as defined in Section 14.5 of the Agreement, shall be excluded from the calculation of Platform availability for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
4\. Service Credit Schedule --- Uptime Failures

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA in any calendar month, Customer shall be entitled to a Service Credit calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment (\$200,000) for the affected calendar month, in accordance with the following tiered schedule:
Monthly Uptime Achieved             Service Credit (% of Monthly Fee)
4A. Service Credit Schedule --- Latency Failures

If p95 latency exceeds 450 ms for any calendar month, an additional Service Credit of 5% of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment (\$10,000) shall apply, subject to the overall monthly cap set forth in Section 5(c).
4B. Service Credit Schedule --- Accuracy Failures

If the F1 score falls below the applicable Model Accuracy target for any measurement period beginning January 1, 2026, an additional Service Credit of 10% of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment (\$20,000) shall apply, subject to the overall monthly cap set forth in Section 5(c).
5\. Service Credit Terms and Conditions

> \(a\) Request Requirement. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor\'s support team within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred. The request must identify the specific dates and times of the SLA failure and reference the applicable monthly service report. Vendor shall validate the claim against its monitoring data and notify Customer of the approved Service Credit amount within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the request.

> \(b\) Application of Credits. Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against the next invoice(s) issued to Customer under the Agreement. If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days.

> \(c\) Maximum Credits. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed twenty percent (20%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month (i.e., \$40,000). Service Credits are cumulative across SLA categories (Uptime, Latency, and Accuracy) but shall not exceed the twenty percent (20%) monthly cap in aggregate. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year.

> \(d\) \*\* Remedies.\*\* Service Credits are not Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5 of the Agreement.
6\. Termination Trigger

If Vendor fails to meet any SLA target (Uptime, Latency, or Accuracy) for three (3) or more consecutive calendar months, Customer may terminate the Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice in accordance with Section 9.5 of the Agreement, without payment of any early termination fee.
